<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Whispering Staff](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2146)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Apex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=10" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Staff" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=151" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 105

**Price** 70,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This gnarled wooden staff is carved with humanoid faces in various emotional states. When the staff is activated, the faces begin to whisper a variety of languages in sibilant tones, creating what seems to be nonsense to all but the staff's wielder or those they choose to affect. The staff functions as a [_major staff of the unblinking eye_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3048). While using the staff, you gain a +3 item bonus to [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=22), [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=24), and [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) checks, regardless of the skill. When you invest the staff, you either increase your Intelligence modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value. You must select the skills and languages the first time you invest the item, and whenever you invest the same _whispering staff_, you get the same skills and languages you chose the first time.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per round;   **Effect** Through the staff's strange whispering, you gain a glimpse into the mind and desires of one creature you can see within 30 feet. Until the end of your next turn, that creature is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) to you and takes a –2 circumstance penalty to saving throws against your spells.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You point the staff at one creature you can see within 30 feet of you, causing the whispers to howl in that creature's mind. The target must attempt a DC 43 Will save. If it fails, whenever the creature attempts an attack roll, skill check, or saving throw, it must roll twice and take the worse roll. This lasts until the start of your next turn.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You twirl the staff in three consecutive circles and call for the whispers to speak up. For the next minute, you and all allies within a 30-foot emanation around you can hear your staff's whispers clearly and distinctly, gaining benefit from their advice and mental protection. Whenever you and your affected allies attempt to Recall Knowledge or attempt a saving throw against a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) effect, you roll twice and take the better result. This is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76) effect.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 119

**Price** 30 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** tattooed on the body

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Geometric precision and perfect angles signify that an artist with exemplary knowledge of [dwarven](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=1) tattooing traditions created this body art. Your family's ancestral stories, recited throughout the tattooing process, bind your blood even tighter to theirs. During your daily preparations, you manifest a visitation by an ancestor—possibly via a dream, a vision, or a magical trinket left by your bedroll. Roll 2d20 and record the highest result. Then roll 1d6 and note a type of saving throw: 1–2 Fortitude, 3–4 Reflex, and 5–6 Will.

 In addition, until the next visitation, you gain a +1 item bonus to one [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) skill related to the ancestor, as determined by the GM. Usually, the ancestor provides a kind of knowledge they believe you'll need. For dwarven ancestors, the Lore skill is usually Architecture Lore, Engineering Lore, Genealogy Lore, Labor Lore, Mining Lore, Warfare Lore, or Lore about a dwarven deity.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You rolled a saving throw of the noted type;  **Effect** Replace the roll with the d20 roll from your ancestor's visitation.

</column>

[Orc](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=19) warriors covet these scar patterns and cluster them around what they consider to be their strongest assets—a pattern around the heart signifies a warrior with great endurance, while one along the arms indicates great upper body strength. 

You gain a +1 item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks. If you have [Ferocity](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=16) (such as from the [Orc Ferocity](/Feats.aspx?ID=83) feat or a similar ability), the first time each day you use it, instead of remaining at 1 Hit Point, your Hit Points are set to an amount equal to your ancestry Hit Points, even if this amount is more than you had before using Ferocity.

Rows of triangles symbolizing shark teeth protect you from danger and enable you to take fierce retaliation against those who try to harm you. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) checks to navigate bodies of water.

Whether the attack hits or misses, you gain a +2 status bonus to damage with the next Strike you make against the attacker before the end of your next turn.

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 122 **Price** 60 gp **Usage** tattooed on the body --- The name of your beloved adorns this stylized image of a heart. An _unbreakable heart_ tattoo can be received only at the end of a successful [_heartbond_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=33) ritual, serving as your token. The other participant can have a token other than a tattoo if they wish. If you have more than one heartbond, each _unbreakable heart_ you have serves as a token for only one of them. The love exuding from you grants you a +1 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks. When you use _heartbond's_ activity to learn your beloved's present state, you can also grant them a small gift, choosing from the following options each time. Make your choice after learning their state.
  • Your beloved gains 5 temporary Hit Points that last for 10 minutes.
  • The tattoo casts [_guidance_](/Spells.aspx?ID=142) on your beloved.
  • The tattoo casts [_stabilize_](/Spells.aspx?ID=307) on your beloved.
  • The tattoo casts [_light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=171) on your beloved's token from _heartbond_.

These tattoos were first created using designs and techniques from the seven Shoanti clans. Each clan is known for one tattoo in particular. The clans would seal alliances in ancient days by tattooing their emblems on members of other clans to symbolically share their gifts. Though these tattoos are respected, the clans reserve their most prestigious symbols for true members of the clan.

The tattoo allows you to understand and speak [Shoanti](/Languages.aspx?ID=171). If you already know that language, you instead gain a +1 item bonus on [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks you make when speaking Shoanti to someone who understands it.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> The actions required to Activate the tattoo are the same as those needed to cast its spell;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The tattoo casts its spell.

These curving, delicate designs resemble leaves, vines, or creepers, most often wrapped around a limb, ear, or throat, or curled around specific muscles. They help you blend in among plants. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks, which increases to +2 in forests.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** A creature would detect you by [Seeking](/Actions.aspx?ID=84); **Requirements** You're in a forest or similar natural area; **Effect** The tattoo casts [_one with plants_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1618) to turn you into a plant before you can be noticed. The duration of this spell is 10 minutes. 

If you’ve already Activated the tattoo, you can supply a separate casting of _one with plants_ to recharge the tattoo instead of having the spell’s normal effect. This allows you to Activate the tattoo again in the same day. You can do so multiple times each day, but only as many times as you continue to cast one with plants to recharge the tattoo after each use.

When you affix the _beastmaster's sigil_, the animal settles into a single form based on where you affix it, showing the animal the item can summon when affixed that way. The spell DC of any spell cast by activating this item is 19. A weapon can benefit from only the melee weapon benefit or ranged weapon benefit.   • **Armor** The sigil grants you a +1 item bonus to saving throws against [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126).
  • **Melee Weapon** The sigil grants you a +1 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks to [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40).
  • **Ranged Weapon** If you critically hit with the affixed weapon, and the target is adjacent to a creature summoned with the sigil, the target takes 1d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29).

When played, no matter what rhythm, it always gives the impression of a marching beat, invoking armies on the move. >
[Alchemist's Haversack](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2305)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Extradimensional" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=67" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 145

**Price** 1,400 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn backpack

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

An _alchemist’s haversack_ is a sturdy leather backpack with two compartments. The main section contains an extradimensional space equivalent to a [spacious pouch type II](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3032), perfect for carrying bulkier alchemist equipment. A secondary partition can hold 2 Bulk of items, 1 of which doesn’t count against your Bulk limit. This second compartment can also be activated (see below).

Two shoulder straps and a thick belt for the waist hold the haversack on the wearer securely. These straps have pouches and loops for keeping alchemical items handy. They also contain magically [expanded alchemist’s toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2702) that grants you a +2 item bonus to [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) checks to create alchemical items.

Water and undesirable material can’t seep into the haversack, which cleans itself once per hour. When you reach in any part of the haversack, the item you sought is the first one you find. Also, the haversack preserves mundane ingredients, food, and drink inside, so they stay fresh indefinitely. This feature doesn’t prolong the duration of magic or alchemical items.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You can create versatile vials; **Effect** You pull a versatile vial from the satchel’s secondary compartment. It’s as effective as the vials you create at the start of the day, not limited like ones created using [Quick Alchemy](/Actions.aspx?ID=2801).

**Craft Requirements** You are an [alchemist](/Classes.aspx?ID=1).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

A _vaultbreaker's harness_ has four pockets across the chest. The pockets contain a set of [infiltrator's thieves' tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=58), infiltrator picks, a [levered crowbar](/Equipment.aspx?ID=18), and a [glass cutter](/Equipment.aspx?ID=870). These items are magically bound to the harness; if they are more than 1 foot away from you, they disappear, then reappear in the harness at the next sunset. [Broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=2) or destroyed items similarly reappear, restored, in their proper pockets at sunset.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You cinch the harness to prepare for mischief. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks and a +10-foot item bonus to your Speed for 1 minute.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You focus on your environment and the creatures around you to see them as they really are. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn eyepiece

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Anything viewed through these thin spectacles looks crisp and clear, and the earpieces accentuate sounds around you. You gain a +2 item bonus to Perception checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** The spectacles key in on someone to show you their social cues in perfect clarity. Choose a creature you can see. You gain a +3 item bonus on Perception checks you make to use [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=85) against that creature. This benefit lasts until you Activate the item again in this way.

 If you’re an [investigator](/Classes.aspx?ID=59), you can use this activation as part of the [Devise a Stratagem](/Actions.aspx?ID=2813) action (even if you’re doing it as a free action). Alternatively, you can use it as part of the [Pursue a Lead](/Actions.aspx?ID=2811) activity, even though you can’t see the creature. This lush velvet capelet is embroidered with images of musicians playing a wide variety of instruments. The images animate when you make art, remaining embroidered, but smoothly unknitting and reknitting in time with your performance. The figures play music that perfectly accompanies your instrument, voice, or movements, granting you a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can use only to cast a bard [composition](/Traits.aspx?ID=31) spell. If not used by the end of your turn, this Focus Point is lost.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You peel the musicians from the garment and fling them around you. The cloak casts a 4th-rank [_phantom crowd_](/Spells.aspx?ID=968) spell (DC 28); each of the 10-foot squares must be adjacent to you. The crowd looks like the musicians on the garment and continues to accompany your Performance checks. You can Sustain this effect as described in the spell.

**Craft Requirements** You are a [bard](/Classes.aspx?ID=3).

The most devoted, [cloistered clerics](/Doctrines.aspx?ID=2) wear a _cloister robe_. Decorations symbolic of a specific deity adorn the robe, and the robe's colors and the complexity of its construction fit the deity's outlook. The robe serves as a [religious symbol](/Equipment.aspx?ID=41) of that deity, and it doesn't need to be wielded to provide that benefit.

 The robe is _+1 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [explorer's clothing](/Armor.aspx?ID=2)_ and grants a +1 item bonus to [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) checks. The robe doesn't grant any benefits to a wearer who doesn't worship the deity tied to the robe. In addition, when you cast a domain spell from one of the deity's domains, you gain resistance to damage from [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48) spells until the end of your next turn. This resistance is equal to half the robe's level.

**Craft Requirements** You are a [cleric](/Classes.aspx?ID=5) who worships the deity tied to the robe.

A _dragon rune bracelet_ is a gold bangle formed around the scale of a famous [dragon](/Traits.aspx?ID=50). The bracelet is etched with esoteric symbols or words in [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2) that indicate kinship with dragons. As many types of _dragon rune bracelet_ exist as there are types of dragons, though bracelets associated with [uncommon](/Traits.aspx?ID=159) or [rare](/Traits.aspx?ID=137) dragons have the same rarity as the dragon.

 While wearing a _dragon rune bracelet_, you gain a +2 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks while interacting with dragons of the same type as the bracelet's scale (such as [red dragons](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=168)  or [cloud dragons](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=176)). You also gain a +2 item bonus to saving throws against [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68) effects from any kind of dragon.

text: Item 11 Dragon Rune Bracelet Focused Invested Magical Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 148, Pathfinder #171: Hurricane's Howl pg. 75 Price 1,400 gp Usage worn A dragon rune bracelet is a gold bangle formed around the scale of a famous dragon. The bracelet is etched with esoteric symbols or words in Draconic that indicate kinship with dragons. As many types of dragon rune bracelet exist as there are types of dragons, though bracelets associated with uncommon or rare dragons have the same rarity as the dragon. While wearing a dragon rune bracelet , you gain a +2 item bonus to Diplomacy checks while interacting with dragons of the same type as the bracelet's scale (such as red dragons or cloud dragons). You also gain a +2 item bonus to saving throws against fear effects from any kind of dragon. Activate Free Action (concentrate) Frequency once per day; Effect You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can spend only to cast a sorcerer draconic bloodline spell. If not used by the end of your turn, this Focus Point is lost. Craft Requirements You are a sorcerer of a draconic bloodline.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 11"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Eidolon Cape](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2323)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Focused" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=74" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 148

**Price** 1,400 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn cloak

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Though it appears to be one elegant piece, an _eidolon cape_ consists of a mantle for your shoulders and a detachable cape. The cape is designed to resemble your [eidolon](/Eidolons.aspx), either with a direct likeness or with features reminiscent of your eidolon. For instance, if your eidolon is a [dragon](/Traits.aspx?ID=50), the cape might depict a stylized dragon, or it might have a pattern of colorful scales with gold trim. An eidolon cape features the sigil you share with your eidolon prominently in its design. You gain a +2 item bonus to the skill that matches your eidolon's tradition: [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) for [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) for [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) for [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), or [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) for [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134).

 When you [Manifest your Eidolon](/Actions.aspx?ID=757), the cape transforms into the eidolon, and when the eidolon unmanifests, it turns back into the cape. If the cape is attached to the mantle, it comes free immediately, and the eidolon appears adjacent to you as normal. If not, the eidolon appears in a space adjacent to the cape. With the cape detached, the mantle is still light Bulk, and the whole cloak remains invested. If the cape is out of range (beyond 100 feet, typically) or there's not enough open space for the eidolon to manifest, your attempt to Manifest your Eidolon fails.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can use only to cast a summoner link spell. If not used by the end of your turn, this Focus Point is lost.

**Craft Requirements** You are a [summoner](/Classes.aspx?ID=18).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>
name: Eidolon Cape

For instance, if your eidolon is a dragon, the cape might depict a stylized dragon, or it might have a pattern of colorful scales with gold trim. An eidolon cape features the sigil you share with your eidolon prominently in its design. You gain a +2 item bonus to the skill that matches your eidolon's tradition: Arcana for arcane, Religion for divine, Occultism for occult, or Nature for primal. When you Manifest your Eidolon, the cape transforms into the eidolon, and when the eidolon unmanifests, it turns back into the cape. If the cape is attached to the mantle, it comes free immediately, and the eidolon appears adjacent to you as normal. If not, the eidolon appears in a space adjacent to the cape. With the cape detached, the mantle is still light Bulk, and the whole cloak remains invested. If the cape is out of range (beyond 100 feet, typically) or there's not enough open space for the eidolon to manifest, your attempt to Manifest your Eidolon fails. Activate Free Action (concentrate) Frequency once per day; Effect You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can use only to cast a summoner link spell. If not used by the end of your turn, this Focus Point is lost. Craft Requirements You are a summoner.

Dangling from a simple cord, a _hexing jar_ houses rich soil. When a [witch](/Classes.aspx?ID=16) who has invested the jar wears it overnight, a miniature thing grows from the soil. Your patron chooses the form, commonly including glowing mushrooms, venus flytraps, mandragora roots, or undead hands reaching up. The thing whispers secrets it learned from your patron, giving you a +2 item bonus to your patron skill.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can use only to cast a witch [hex](/Traits.aspx?ID=324) spell. If not used by the end of your turn, this Focus Point is lost.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** You roll a critical success on an attack roll with a witch spell, or your target rolls a critical failure on its saving throw against a witch spell or hex you cast;  **Effect** The thing in the jar becomes more energetic—glowing, dancing, rapping on the glass, or some other action appropriate to its appearance. It encourages you until the start of your next turn, granting you and your familiar a +1 status bonus to AC and saving throws and a +2 status bonus against [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) effects.

**Craft Requirements** You are a witch.

A thin wooden mask carved in the shape of a skull, monstrous face, or eerily featureless visage, a mask of uncanny breath fully covers your face. While wearing it, each breath you take feels cool and pure, perfectly flowing to feed your qi. You gain resistance 10 to [inhaled](/Traits.aspx?ID=96) [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) and can breathe in an airless or toxic environment. When you breathe in, fragments of bizarre knowledge flow through you, granting you a +2 item bonus to [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can use only to cast an [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120) monk qi spell. If not used by the end of your turn, this Focus Point is lost.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** Your [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) Strike hits a creature that breathes;  **Effect** The mask contorts and inhales, sucking breath from your target's lungs. The target falls [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) but doesn't fall [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) or drop what it's holding. It wakes up at the end of your turn if it hasn't been woken up already.

**Craft Requirements** You are a [monk](/Classes.aspx?ID=8) with occult qi spells.

Gemstones of many colors adorn the silver of a _mind's light circlet_. When you're charged with mental power, the jewels scintillate with light, with different gems resonating based on your emotions. If you have at least 1 Focus Point, the gems cast [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) in a 10-foot radius. When you amp a spell, the light increases to [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in a 20-foot radius (and dim light to the next 20 feet) until the start of your next turn.

 You gain a +2 item bonus to [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) checks. You also gain the following [amp](/Traits.aspx?ID=425), which you can apply to any of your psi cantrips that have a target or area, much like an amp gained from a feat.

 **Amp** You transfer some of the magical luminescence from the mind's light circlet to one of the creatures. Choose a creature targeted by the spell or in its area. Until the start of your next turn, that creature sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius (and dim light to the next 20 feet) and can't be [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4). If the creature is [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26), it's concealed while alight, rather than being [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39).

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can use only to use a psychic amp. If not used by the end of your turn, this Focus Point is lost.

**Craft Requirements** You are a [psychic](/Classes.aspx?ID=21).

>
[Crown of the Companion](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2334)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=89" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Vitality" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=509" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 151, [Pathfinder #170: Spoken on the Song Wind](/Sources.aspx?ID=97) pg. 75

**Price** 250 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Stories tell of a king who once loved his subjects so much he was willing to give his own life energy for them, using an object like the _crown of the companion_. Whether true or not, this majestic wooden crown bears elaborate carvings depicting that tale with images of a regal figure giving increasingly of themself to a throng of needy subjects. While wearing this crown, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You bow to an ally within 30 feet, creating a magical bond between the two of you as if you cast [_share life_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1669) targeting the ally. The link remains even if you move more than 30 feet away from them. At the end of the spell’s duration, your ally recovers 4d8 Hit Points and you recover half of what they recover.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>
name: Crown of the Companion

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 151 **Price** 220 gp **Usage** worn headwear **Bulk** L --- Made of materials scavenged from wild places, a _druid's crown_ can be rebuilt for a variety of benefits. The crown grants you a +1 item bonus to a skill, and can be activated to cast a spell, both depending on the material used to build the crown, as listed on the table below. If you invest and wear [_living mantle_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3092) along with the crown, the crown's item bonus increases by 1 and its spell's DC rises to 27. You can invest this item only if you're a [druid](/Classes.aspx?ID=6). When you do, as a 10-minute activity that has the [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104) trait, you can disassemble and rebuild the crown with different materials, changing its item bonus and spell accordingly. ##
**Material****Item Bonus****Spell**
Antlers[Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7)[_Enlarge_](/Spells.aspx?ID=102)
Flowers[Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6)[_Animal allies_](/Spells.aspx?ID=863)
Leaves[Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15)[_One with Plants_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1618)
 **Activate** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The crown casts its spell at 2nd rank (DC 20). **Craft Requirements** You are a druid.
name: Druid's Crown

A _hunter's arrowhead_ is meant to be worn as a charm, such as a pendant, or carried in a pocket or quiver. While you wear or carry the arrowhead, it infuses you with great skill at hunting, and you gain a +1 item bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) checks and attack rolls against any creature you've currently designated as your prey with [Hunt Prey](/Actions.aspx?ID=10). A _hunter's arrowhead_ is also a [religious symbol](/Equipment.aspx?ID=41) of Ketephys.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You would miss with an attack made with a [bow](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=3);  **Effect** You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your attack roll, possibly turning a miss into a hit.

The opal set in the intricately carved ivory _spiritsight ring_ eventually becomes translucent and tickles your finger whenever an [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) creature is nearby. When in the presence of a nearby incorporeal creature, even if it's within a solid object, you eventually detect the creature, though you might not do so instantly, and you can't pinpoint the location. This acts as a [vague sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=413), like humans' sense of smell. An incorporeal creature trying to hide its presence from this sense attempts a [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) check against your Perception DC to hide from your vague sense, as normal for attempting to foil [special senses](/Rules.aspx?ID=414). You gain a +2 item bonus when using the [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) action to find [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) incorporeal creatures within 30 feet of you.

If you roll a success or critical success, you can repeat what the _Whisperer of Souls_ relates to you about the subject. On a critical failure, you and the glaive are drawn into a murmuring void of cold, where your mind is assaulted by strange visions for an entire week. At the end of this time, you reappear and must attempt a DC 50 Will save. **Success** When you return, you can retrain one of your skills into a [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) skill about evil creatures or places, as if you had spent 1 week retraining.

You must retrain one of your skills into a Lore about unholy creatures or places. You become obsessed with increasing your forbidden knowledge, turning to wicked forces that offer such secrets and compromising your morals further if you must. **Destruction** If the _Whisperer of Souls_ is used to slay [Shelyn's](/Deities.aspx?ID=17) [herald](/Traits.aspx?ID=330), it disintegrates, bringing about great evil in its wake.

_Note from Nethys: This item is a constituent part of the [Ursine Avenger Hood](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=200) archetype using the [archetype artifact](/Rules.aspx?ID=1961) rules._

A gift passed from warrior to warrior, this cowl is made from a [cave bear's](/Monsters.aspx?ID=48) skull and fur. **Destruction** Soak the _Ursine Avenger Hood_ in the blood of a [linnorm](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=69) that is at least 16th level and then burn it in a fire that uses only oak and chrysanthemum as fuel.

</title>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 190

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn garment

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +20; [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=2406) vision 30 feet, [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=2407) hearing 30 feet

**Communication** [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) ([Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155), [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115), four other languages)

**Skills** [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +21, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +19, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +19

**Int** +2, **Wis** +5, **Cha** +4

**Will** +20 

</column>

---        

Devotees of benevolent faiths fear and loathe corruption cassocks, each of which is dedicated to an [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) deity. When the garment chooses a target, such as when it senses a worshipper of a deity who isn’t unholy, it alters its form to match another deity’s iconography, appearing to be a devoted vestments for that deity. Once donned, the cassock tries to subtly sway its wearer to the worship of its deity. If the wearer begins to succumb, the _corruption cassock_ gradually reverts to its true appearance, replacing its false iconography as its wearer converts.

A _corruption cassock_ functions as a [_devoted vestments_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3077) for any wearer it chooses. Once you invest the cassock, it fuses to you. While you remain loyal to another deity, you believe the cassock grants you a +2 item bonus to [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) checks and a +1 item bonus to the divine skill of the deity to whom you believe the cassock is dedicated. It does neither. The GM secretly adjusts your checks with those skills, causing you to fail at religious tasks more often. If you have multiple equal or lower item bonuses to the affected skills, the cassock takes precedence, negating those bonuses. If you convert to following the cassock’s true unholy deity, however, these bonuses function normally for you.

If you attempt to Cast a Spell that has the [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) trait, the cassock can force you to attempt a DC 28 Will save. On a failure, you’re [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 for one minute (stupefied 2 on a critical failure). A _corruption cassock_ uses this ability to convince you that your deity has forsaken you.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can spend only to cast a  cleric domain spell for a domain belonging to the deity you believe the cassock is dedicated to. If you don't spend this Focus Point by the end of this turn, it's lost. However, when you use this activation, the _corruption cassock_ can instead cast a domain spell of the same rank from its deity. It does so only to confuse and dismay you, harming your faith.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

Activate Single Action (concentrate) Effect You take a –10-foot penalty to your Speed for 1 minute, and the bracelet fuses to you. Thereafter, it grants you no bonus to Acrobatics checks, and it imposes a –5-foot status penalty to your Speed.

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

</row>

</column>

---

An _unfathomable stargazer_ is a handheld brass telescope etched with constellations, the patterns of which form bizarre, shifting runes. You can observe the night sky with an _unfathomable stargazer_, however, the constellations you glimpse through the telescope distort with expanding and contracting fields of darkness among them. You use [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) instead of Perception or [Astronomy Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) when observing the skies with this item, and gain a +2 item bonus on all checks to do so. Once you use it, it fuses to you, and you must succeed at a DC 35 Will save to use another device to observe the stars, including your naked eyes. The telescope imposes a –4 circumstance penalty to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) checks to [Sense Direction](/Actions.aspx?ID=64) or navigate. If you critically fail this Survival check, you're subjected to [_warp mind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=369) (DC 34) as you glimpse something horrifying and alien amid the darkness.

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +13; [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) vision 30 feet, [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) hearing 30 feet

**Communication** speech ([Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) and 1 imparted language)

**Skills** [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +13, [Nobility Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +13, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +13

**Int** +3, **Wis** +3, **Cha** +3

</column>

---        

Forged in platinum, a _majordomo torc_ is engraved with heraldic insignias along with one language's alphabet, much like a [_choker of elocution_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=422). You gain a +1 item bonus to [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) checks and the ability to understand, speak, and write the torc's language. Your excellent elocution reduces the DC of the flat check to perform an auditory action while [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) from 5 to 3.

 Upon being invested, the torc appoints itself your majordomo and, given the chance, takes over coordinating your social calendar, engagements, and wardrobe. A _majordomo torc_ has a prim, fussy disposition, and although it defers to you, it can grow sardonic if you frequently ignore its advice. The torc has the following activation.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The _majordomo torc_ casts [_befitting attire_](/Spells.aspx?ID=867) on you, usually to your specifications. However the torc can also choose the appearance of the illusion for you.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="No Alignment" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
<trait label="Focused" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=74" />

<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 196

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** 2 hands

**Bulk** 16
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +22; [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) vision 30 feet, [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) hearing 30 feet

**Communication** [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=37) (any languages the possessing spirit knew in life)

**Skills** [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +23, [Music Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +23, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) +25, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +21

**Int** +3, **Wis** +4, **Cha** +5

**Will** +22 

</column>

---        

When a skilled musician dies before reaching their full potential or accomplishing an important goal, their soul might refuse to move on to the [Boneyard](/Planes.aspx?ID=15). Rather than becoming [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), the spirit possesses an instrument they played in life, turning it into an intelligent item and a [virtuoso instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=37). (Other _phantom instruments_ exist, but most are heavy.) A _phantom piano_ offers a bargain to any bard or other skilled musician who finds it: receive musical aid as you dedicate yourself to reaching the success the spirit felt they were denied in life. The piano refuses to play for those who reject this deal. If you accept, the piano asks only that you practice with it and perform for increasingly refined and august audiences, requiring a successful [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) check appropriate to your proficiency level. The piano sets no strict timeline, but at the GM's discretion, if you go too long without making progress, the piano can cease cooperating with you until it's satisfied with your dedication once again.

 While you keep up your end of the bargain, the piano grants you a +2 item bonus to Performance checks made with it. The piano also provides access to composition spells based on your Performance proficiency rank, as if you had the corresponding feat. The spells you can use comprise a cumulative list, but you can cast them only when using the piano. You must spend the actions and Focus Points required to cast these spells.

**Trained**  [_courageous anthem_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1763), [_uplifting overture_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1779)

**Expert**  [hymn of healing](/Feats.aspx?ID=4574), [_rallying anthem_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1773)

**Master**  [_symphony of the unfettered heart_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1777)

**Legendary**  [_soothing ballad_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1776)

 A _phantom piano_ has the following activations.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** The piano shrinks down to a figurine of light Bulk compact enough to store in a pouch, or from figurine form back to instrument form. In figurine form, the piano doesn't function as an instrument or provide magic other than this activation.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can spend only to Cast a Spell the piano provides you.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 204 **Usage** worn --- Blessed by [Nivi Rhombodazzle](/Deities.aspx?ID=44), this striking silver necklace is adorned with sparkling sapphires that draw the eye of any who see it. Over the years, this necklace has appeared in many paintings and illustrations, usually around the neck of a carefree and daring adventurer or a stylish rake gambling vast sums of coin. Finding this relic is always seen as a sign of great fortune to come, but when that luck runs out, the necklace is lost just as quickly. Wearing the relic, you quickly realize how distracting it can be, granting you a +1 item bonus on [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks made to [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=48) and on [Games Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) checks made to gamble or determine the outcome of a game of chance. --- **Minor Gifts**: [beginner's luck](/Relics.aspx?ID=97), [whammy](/Relics.aspx?ID=99)
**Major Gifts**: [clean luck](/Relics.aspx?ID=100), [perception filter](/Relics.aspx?ID=52)
**Grand Gift**: [against all odds](/Relics.aspx?ID=102)

The sleuth's pipe has sapience that eventually awakens, allowing the relic to act as a helpful assistant in investigations. Even while this sapience sleeps within the pipe, it grants you a +1 item bonus to Perception checks to Sense Motive, and if you're an investigator, any checks you make to Pursue a Lead. Minor Gifts : beginner's luck, repository of knowledge Major Gifts : intelligent relic, steal luck Grand Gift : mental bastion

item_bonus_note: Recall Knowledge about historical subjects
markdown:
**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 205 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L --- The origins of the _watch of lost ages_, a silver pocket watch, are enigmatic. Its construction matches no known culture, and its appearance shifts back and forth from battered and tarnished to shiny and new without cause or apparent reason. The watch exudes a sense of melancholy and loss, and anyone holding it is acutely aware of the impermanence of all things and the march of time, moving ever forward. This relic might show up in a mysterious ruin or spontaneously appear in a spellcaster's hand after they cast a time spell. The relic grants you a +1 item bonus to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) about historical subjects. --- **Minor Gifts**: [fervor](/Relics.aspx?ID=93), [sands of the hourglass](/Relics.aspx?ID=104)
**Major Gifts**: [fervent spell](/Relics.aspx?ID=95), [temporal pulse](/Relics.aspx?ID=106)
**Grand Gift**: [time reversal](/Relics.aspx?ID=108)

Astrolabes can be used for navigation in unfamiliar or featureless locations. To use an astrolabe, the holder must be trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16). An eyecatcher is a simple tassel, reflective basket hilt, or other accessory attached to a weapon to serve as a distraction. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=48) while using a weapon with an eyecatcher attached. An eyecatcher affects the balancing of a weapon, making it slightly more unwieldy. This increases the weapon's Bulk by 1 and grants a –1 penalty to damage rolls with the weapon.

Using fabrics and fashion accessories, you disguise your armor to look like everyday clothing. After applying this adjustment, you can attempt a [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) check to [Conceal an Object](/Actions.aspx?ID=61) to hide the nature of your armor. You gain a +1 item bonus to this check. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 84

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn shoes

**Bulk** 1
</row>

**Access** Second-mark members of the Firebrands have access to this item.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These comfortable and practical boots slip on easily and fill you with boundless energy. The treads of these boots provide exceptional traction, with improved grip on surfaces you would traditionally have difficulty traversing. While wearing the boots, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) checks to [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=28) and to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks to [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=36) and [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=37).

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The traction of your boots improves, allowing you to run along vertical surfaces for 1 minute. When you Stride, you can run up solid vertical surfaces, like walls, at your full Speed. You must start your movement on a horizontal surface. If you end a Stride off the ground, you must Stride along the surface again until you reach a horizontal surface or you begin to fall (though you can [Grab an Edge](/Actions.aspx?ID=95), if applicable). If you have means of walking on water, such as with [_water walk_](/Spells.aspx?ID=371) or similar abilities, you can also run along flimsy vertical surfaces, as well as vertical liquids such as a waterfall.

These black leather gloves fit snuggly, running up the length of your arm to your elbow. Each glove has an angular fin running along the outside edge of your arms, which forms a narrow triangle when your hands meet in a diving position. While wearing the gloves, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks to [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=39).

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision;   **Trigger** You would take [damage from falling](/Rules.aspx?ID=402) into water;  **Effect** The gloves create a hydrodynamic barrier around you, dispersing the damage that would be done to you during a high dive. You take damage as if the fall were half the distance, to a minimum fall of 5 feet. You then Swim with the effects of a critical success for the check.

[Stone of Encouragement](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2467)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 87

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access** Second-mark members of the Firebrands have access to this item.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This smooth, round, gray stone fits neatly into the palm of your hand and feels comfortable to hold regardless of the size or shape of your hand. While you're holding the stone, it telepathically speaks to you at regular intervals in generic words of encouragement, such as “You can do it!” and “Let's go!” The encouraging words manifest in the voice of your internal monologue or take on the characteristics of the voice of someone you trust. Despite the similarity, you're aware that the stone is telepathically projecting its voice and can differentiate between the stone's voice and your internal monologue or the voice of the person you trust.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You ask the stone for help with a task. It speaks a few motivating words related to the task at hand, which grants you a +1 item bonus to the first skill check you attempt within 1 minute. You become temporarily immune to the effects of all _stones of encouragement_, even ones other than the one you activated, for 1 day. You can still hear the encouraging words of different stones if you hold them, but they don't provide any benefits.

May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate **Source** [Pathfinder #190: The Choosing](/Sources.aspx?ID=198) pg. 77, [Stolen Fate Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=197) pg. 5 **Usage** carried --- _The Empty Throne_ represents great loss and wisdom from those who are now gone. As long as you have _The Empty Throne_ invested, it grants you a +2 item bonus to [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) and [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) checks made to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) regarding individuals who are no longer alive (such as checks to learn about Taldor's historical founder, but not to learn about its current empress). This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level. **Activate** envision; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You overwhelm a target you can see within 60 feet with feelings of helplessness and loss. The creature must attempt a Will DC equal to your class DC. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The target can't benefit from circumstance or status bonuses for 1 round.
**Failure** The target can't benefit from circumstance or status bonuses for 1 day, and the target's allies are unable to benefit from circumstance or status bonuses while within 15 feet of the target.
**Critical Failure** As failure, except the duration is 1 week.

_The Fiend_ represents the inevitability of great calamities and pervasive dangers. As long as you have _The Fiend_ invested, when you repeat a non-Strike action you previously took in the same round, you gain a +2 item bonus to checks to perform that action. This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You wave the card to create a vision of destruction around you; you cast [_phantasmal calamity_](/Spells.aspx?ID=218), except the area is a 20-foot emanation. The level of the spell is one-half your level, rounded down (minimum 6th level), and the save DC is your class DC. You are immune to the effects of your own _phantasmal calamity_.

_The Liar_ represents obsession or treacherous love. As long as you have _The Liar_ invested, it grants you a +2 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47). This increases to a +3 item bonus if you're at least 17th level. If the implausibility of your lies prompts a circumstance penalty to your Deception checks or an increase to your Deception DC, reduce that penalty or increase by half.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You touch a weapon and instill faithlessness within it. The weapon gains the [backbiting curse](/Curses.aspx?ID=3). The curse lasts until you use this activation again. If you're at least 17th level, you can instead use this activation on a weapon within 30 feet. If the weapon is carried by a creature, it can resist the effect with a successful Will save against your class DC.

_The Rakshasa_ represents domination of others to support your own schemes. When you invest _The Rakshasa_, identify a single willing creature within 30 feet as your pledged follower. If you're at least 15th level, you can have up to two pledged followers at once. At 18th level, you can have up to three pledged followers. If you have the maximum pledged followers active and select a new one, a previous pledged follower of your choice is no longer your pledged follower. You gain an item bonus equal to your current number of pledged followers to all [Coerce](/Actions.aspx?ID=52) attempts.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" />  ;  **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** You regain Hit Points equal to twice your level, and a pledged follower of your choice loses Hit Points equal to your level (no effects apply that would decrease this Hit Point loss). If this loss kills your pledged follower, you also gain temporary Hit Points equal to your level. The pledged follower is temporarily immune to this activation for 24 hours.

_The Marriage_ symbolizes a union of body, mind, spirit, or any of the three. When _The Marriage_ is invested, you gain a +2 item bonus to attempts made to [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=51). This increases to a +3 item bonus at 17th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Choose one adjacent willing creature. By brushing _The Marriage_ against their body, you form a magical bond with that creature that persists until you activate _The Marriage_ again to form a bond with a different creature. While the bond persists, you and the other creature can communicate via [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=37) to a distance of 120 feet. As long as you and the target are on the same plane of existence and are both alive, you each remain aware of the other's state—you know the other's direction from you, distance from you, and any conditions affecting them. If your bonded target becomes [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1), [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=5), [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=6), [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=14), [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19), [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35), or [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36), you can use a reaction to attempt to [counter](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the condition affecting the target, which also ends the bond between you and the target. The modifier on this counter check is equal to your class DC – 10. If you fail to counter the condition, that condition also afflicts you, and the bond with the other still ends.

When The Marriage is invested, you gain a +2 item bonus to attempts made to Request. This increases to a +3 item bonus at 17th level. Activate Two Actions envision, Interact; Frequency once per day; Effect Choose one adjacent willing creature. By brushing The Marriage against their body, you form a magical bond with that creature that persists until you activate The Marriage again to form a bond with a different creature. While the bond persists, you and the other creature can communicate via telepathy to a distance of 120 feet. As long as you and the target are on the same plane of existence and are both alive, you each remain aware of the other's state—you know the other's direction from you, distance from you, and any conditions affecting them. If your bonded target becomes blinded, confused, controlled, fascinated, frightened, slowed, or stunned, you can use a reaction to attempt to counter the condition affecting the target, which also ends the bond between you and the target. The modifier on this counter check is equal to your class DC – 10. If you fail to counter the condition, that condition also afflicts you, and the bond with the other still ends.

These brilliant golden bracers feature a hammer motif as part of their engravings. While wearing them, your body surges with strength and you gain a +3 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks and a +1 circumstance bonus to Athletics checks to [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41) and [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40). If you succeed, but not critically succeed, at your check to Disarm a creature, the effects of your check last until the start of your next turn, instead until the start of the target's turn. If you succeed at a check to Trip a creature, it takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage or 4d6 bludgeoning damage on a critical success. When you invest the bracers, you either increase your Strength score by 2 or increase it to 18, whichever would give you a higher score.

Attempt an Athletics check to Trip a creature within reach. On a success, the creature is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) and takes 10d6 bludgeoning damage (double on a critical hit). If you knock the creature prone, it must also attempt a DC 35 Reflex save. On a failure, it drops any items it's holding.

---

This simple, tattered cloak is a faded green and features small, stylized keys sewn throughout its length. While wearing the cloak, you fade into the shadows and gain a +3 item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks. When you invest the cloak, you either increase your Dexterity score by 2 or increase it to 18, whichever would give you a higher score.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You brush your hand against the cloak and your fingers transform into picks, tension wrenches, skeleton keys, and any other tools, providing you with a full set of [thieves' tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=58). This transformation doesn't otherwise hamper the normal use of your fingers or hands. These tools never break when you critically fail your check to [Pick a Lock](/Actions.aspx?ID=70). You can Activate the cloak again to revert your fingers to normal.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You place your hand against a wall, floor, or ceiling. You create a magical doorway within the surface that a creature can move through, as if the door had always been there. The doorway can penetrate up to 10 feet of material; particularly thick material, such as heavy stone walls, can cause this effect to fail, expending its use for the day. You can use an Interact action on the door to remove it from the surface and return it to its previous shape.

---

This elegant black sash features stylized crimson books embroidered at either end and a set of simple tassels. While wearing the sash, you feel as if you have a better understanding of the people and life around you. You gain a +3 item bonus to [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) checks.

 When you invest the sash, you either increase your Intelligence score by 2 or increase it to 18, whichever would give you a higher score.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** You focus on a creature you can see and attempt to gain an instinctual understanding of the creature. You attempt a check to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) about the creature, rolling twice and taking the higher result. If you roll a critical failure on this check, you get a failure instead. Regardless of the result, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to attack rolls against the creature and to your AC and saving throws against attacks and effects from the creature for 1 minute. This bonus increases to +2 if you critically succeeded your check to Recall Knowledge.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You become keenly aware of your surroundings and become able to anticipate dangers. You gain the effects of [_foresight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=127).

---

_The Betrayal_ represents selfishness and envy, twisting outcomes toward unfavorable or even devastating results. As long as _The Betrayal_ is invested, you become more adept at hiding who you really are and tricking targets into positions of vulnerability. You gain a +2 item bonus on [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks made to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) or [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=48). This increases to a +3 bonus if you are at least 17th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You turn the tables on your foes, bringing one of them into your ranks and compelling them to attack their allies. You cast [_dominate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=87) on a creature, but can only issue commands to attack or otherwise harm, betray, or inconvenience its allies. The level of the spell is one-half your level, rounded down (minimum 6th level), and the save DC is your class DC.

Activate Free Action envision, Interact (teleportation) Frequency once per day; Effect You hold the card in your hand, and with a flick of the wrist it vanishes, only to be replaced by an object of your choice within 30 feet. _The Unicorn_ represents finding what one seeks. As long as you have _The Unicorn_ invested, you gain a +2 item bonus on Perception checks to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84). This increases to a +3 item bonus if you're at least 17th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You pass _The Unicorn_ across an adjacent closed container and then open the container. Inside, you'll find a Common [consumable](/Traits.aspx?ID=36) alchemical or magic item you need to solve a problem or deal with a situation close at hand. For example, if you're badly wounded, you might find a [_greater healing potion_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=186). If you've been poisoned, you could discover a [_panacea_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=188). If you're faced with a written clue in a language you don't understand, the container might hold a [comprehension elixir](/Equipment.aspx?ID=88). The GM always decides what consumable item is discovered, and it must be equal to or lower than your level. If the consumable isn't used within 1 minute of being discovered, the item vanishes. If there's no appropriate item to solve your situation, the GM can rule that no object is found; in this case, the daily use of _The Unicorn_ is not expended.

The thick gloves are designed to help ranchers hold on to the squirming, slimy bodies of grindlegrubs, and help soothe the wear and tear of the day while restoring energy for after-hours pursuits. While wearing the gloves, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks. The gripping power of the gloves provides you with a +2 circumstance bonus to Reflex saves to [Grab an Edge](/Actions.aspx?ID=95). If you roll a success to Grab an Edge, you get a critical success instead, as the _gripping gloves_ allow you to hold on even with just a few fingertips.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You rub your hands together and take a deep breath to prepare for the rest of your day. You regain 3d8+10 Hit Points and feel refreshed, losing the [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15) condition. As normal for effects that remove fatigue, this doesn't remove any underlying source of fatigue, such as lack of sleep, causing the condition to return if the underlying source isn't addressed.

It can be played as an instrument, granting a +2 item bonus to your [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) check. **Activate** Interact; **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** Blowing into the horn with destructive intent, you create a blast note targeting one creature within 30 feet. The blast deals 3d6 sonic damage (DC 28 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save). **Activate** Interact; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You blow even louder to create an intense blast wave in a 30-foot cone that deals 8d6 sonic damage. Each creature attempts a DC 28 Fortitude save with the following effects **Critical Success** The creature takes no damage.
**Success** The creature takes half damage.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage and is deafened for 2d6 rounds.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Air" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=5" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 74

**Price** 60 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn cloak

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This blue cloak is surprisingly light for its length and seems to catch wind bursts in its tail, flying out behind the wearer while cushioning falls and easing jumps. The sides of the cloak are slightly weighted, making it easy to grab ahold of when it fills with air. This cloak grants you a +1 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks to [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=81) and a +1 item bonus to Acrobatics checks to [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=28) or [Maneuver in Flight](/Actions.aspx?ID=30).

**Activate—Fall Gently** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You're [falling](/Rules.aspx?ID=401);  **Effect** The cloak catches the air and you grab onto its edges, utilizing the draft to guide you to safety. Treat your fall as 30 feet shorter and glide to a space of your choice at the bottom of your fall, which must be within 20 feet of where you would've landed.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 75

**Price** 900 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn belt

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

This scarf is made of fine silk that's the same shade of blue as a clear, cloudless sky. The long edges have exquisite embroidery in threads that vary from a blue identical to the silk to the deep gray of storm clouds during winter. **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 99 **Price** 1,800 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand --- _Jabali's dice_ are two six-sided dice carved from evenly weighted stone to the specifications of a specific jabali shuyookh. The sides showing a 6 also have the name and title of the shuyookh inscribed in Petran. If you whisper the name and title during a dice game using _jabali's dice_, they bless you with a bit of luck, granting a +2 item bonus to your [Games Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) check. You can do so frequently enough to apply this bonus while [Earning Income](/Actions.aspx?ID=23) using Games Lore, but only one user at a time can do so. **Activate—Jabali's Gamble** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You call out the shuyookh's name and title, then roll the dice. The shuyookh appears briefly to provide for your defense. Roll 2d6 to determine the effect. Represented by the GM, the shuyookh chooses any effect's specifications, benefiting you according to the shuyookh's whims.
**2–5**The shuyookh casts [_mountain resilience_](/Spells.aspx?ID=312) on you.
**6–9**The shuyookh casts [_grasping earth_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1334), but you and your allies are immune to it.
**10–11**The shuyookh casts [_wall of stone_](/Spells.aspx?ID=365). The edges can pass through creatures, which are shunted to the side of the wall opposite that edge.
**12**The shuyookh casts a DC 31 [_petrify_](/Spells.aspx?ID=123) spell on a creature hostile and in proximity to you. If no appealing target exists, you receive a 10–11 result instead.
name: Jabali's Dice

---

_Ash gowns_ are formal wear spun from smoke, ash, and char collected from the [Plane of Fire](/Planes.aspx?ID=6). Typically, they're voluminous floor-length dresses or three-piece suits, but regardless of their specific tailoring, _ash gowns_ are always an ostentatious display of wealth and loyalty to the powers of the Plane of Fire. They're exceptionally popular in the courts of the [Elemental Lords](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=8) and among the high society of Medina Mudii'a. The gown grants you resistance 5 to fire and a +1 item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks.

**Activate—Blazing Promenade** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The ash gown ignites in a ferocious blaze, flames licking the floor and trailing behind you like a dancing cape. You Stride and make a Strike at the end of your movement. During the Stride, your flames incinerate minor obstacles in your path; you ignore non-magical [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453), and any you move through is destroyed. Creatures that are adjacent to you at any point during your movement take 2d6 fire damage with a DC 23 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. A creature doesn't need to attempt this save more than once, even if you move past it multiple times.

---

This exquisite, shimmering rhyton is made from volcanic glass and encrusted with rubies, garnets, and other red gemstones, with a blown glass sculpture of a snakelike fire elemental at its base. It was sculpted as part of a 10-piece set of drinking horns, created to match a powerful ifrit shuyookh's entertaining dinnerware, but it became separated from the rest of the collection. Whether for good or ill, the beautiful glass rhyton still carries tidings from its previous shuyookh owner, and you become their esteemed guest from afar whenever you hold it.

 The drinking horn functions as a [bottomless stein](/Equipment.aspx?ID=563), refilling with a common ale each time it's emptied. However, anyone holding the rhyton who whispers the name of its former shuyookh owner has the horn filled with their favorite wine, spirit, juice, or other beverage from anywhere across the many planes, as if their wish were granted by a magnanimous genie.

**Activate—Toast!** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))    **Effect** You raise a toast to a creature or creatures you're about to socialize with. You gain a +2 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6), or [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks against those creatures for 1 hour.

**Activate—Ifrit's Command** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** An ifrit's hospitality always comes with an implied threat. You cause the shuyookh to briefly appear and take its vengeance on those who would hurt you, the genie's “guest.” The shuyookh issues a 6th-rank [_command_](/Spells.aspx?ID=45) that targets all creatures [hostile](/Conditions.aspx?ID=23) to you in range instead of the usual number of targets. The shuyookh issues the same command to all of them. Each target that fails its save also feels all nourishment leached from it, becoming [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15) as long as it's affected by the _command_.

</column>

---

_Smoke veils_ are wigs or headdresses made of flame and ash, giving the wearer a burning coil of fiery hair and concealing their face behind a smoldering, omnipresent haze of smoke and sparking embers. You can use the veil to go unrecognized by hiding your face so that you can attempt [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) without needing a [disguise kit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=19). When you do so, it takes you only 1 minute to create the disguise, and you gain a +1 item bonus to the check. You still need a disguise kit and the full time if you're using cosmetics and other props to change other aspects of your disguise, or if Impersonating a specific person.

**Activate—Blazing Stare** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32))   **Requirements** You dealt fire damage to a target you can see within 30 feet with your most recent action this turn; **Effect** You set your fiery gaze on your target, eyes burning within a cloud of ash and cinder. Roll an [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) check to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) the target. Demoralize loses the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16) trait and gains the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163) trait, and you don't take a penalty when you attempt to Demoralize a creature that doesn't understand your language.

Every part of this dark, shining guitar, from the strings to the soundboard, is constructed of metal. When the strings are strummed, the gilding on the guitar ripples like a liquid. A _resonant guitar_ is a [virtuoso handheld musical instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=37) that grants a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks attempted while using it.

 A _resonant guitar_ is a planar key for [_interplanar teleport_](/Spells.aspx?ID=222) and similar magic to travel to the [Plane of Metal](/Planes.aspx?ID=24). When using it in this way, you can play a tune inspired by your destination to make it more likely to arrive where you intend to be, appearing 1d6×25 miles from your intended destination instead of 1d10×25 miles away.

**Activate—Strum of Thunder** <actions string="" /> 1 minute ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You play a magnetic tune, enchanting one metallic weapon within 60 feet of you. This item gains the [_thundering_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=306) rune for 1 hour.

**Activate—Chord of Protection** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** A creature within 30 feet of you targets you or an ally with a melee attack;  **Effect** You strike a piercing chord, putting up an invisible sound barrier between the target and the attacker. The target gains a +2 status bonus to AC against the triggering attack. If the Strike still hits, the barrier breaks, dealing 3d10 sonic damage to the attacker.

</row>

---

An array of semiprecious stones is set into the ornate silver and beaten copper cover of this thick and weighty tome. If you open the book before it’s been activated, its vellum pages are blank and pristine, but once activated, words dance and swim onto the pages before your eyes.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (envision, Interact);     **Effect** As you flip through the book, you think about a broad topic you want to know more about. Choose one skill: Arcana, Crafting, Medicine, Nature, Occultism, Religion, Society, or a single subcategory of Lore. The book’s pages fill with information about that skill, though only you can see the information. While the pages are full, you can spend an Interact action perusing the book just before attempting a check to Recall Knowledge with the chosen skill. This grants you a +3 item bonus to the check, and if you roll a critical failure, you get a failure instead. The information within the book disappears after 24 hours or when the tome is activated again.

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=165" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 176

**Price** 1,850 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Magical writing covers the surface of this beautiful conch shell, which emits a blue light from inside. A _conch of otherworldly seas_ is a [virtuoso handheld musical instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=37) that grants a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks attempted while using it. 

The conch is a planar key for [_interplanar teleport_](/Spells.aspx?ID=222) and similar magic to travel to the [Plane of Water](/Planes.aspx?ID=7). When using it this way, you can attune it to the waters of your destination to make it more likely to arrive where you intend to be, appearing 1d6×25 miles from your intended destination instead of 1d10×25 miles away.

**Activate—Voice of Oceans** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))    **Effect** You hold the horn to your ear and can understand and speak [Thalassic](/Languages.aspx?ID=113) as long as it remains there.

**Activate—Sounds of the Deep** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))    **Effect** You hold the horn to your ear and touch the correct series of runes inscribed on its surface, causing the conch to cast a 5th-rank [_clairaudience_](/Spells.aspx?ID=39) spell for your benefit. Provided you choose a location that's underwater, you can extend the spell's range to 1 mile and hear with perfect clarity.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

Many of the experienced woodcarvers of the [Plane of Wood](/Planes.aspx?ID=25) learn to fight as well, the better to travel into hazardous areas in search of rare and beautiful types of wood for their craft. A _carver-cutter_ serves a dual role as a weapon and a tool for felling trees and engraving wood. The _+2 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [battle axe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=16)_ looks like an exquisitely made woodcutting axe.

**Activate—Carving Chisel** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))    **Effect** You pull free a woodworking chisel stored in the knob of the axe. It can have any standard chisel shape you imagine as you activate this ability. You get a +2 item bonus to [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) checks for woodworking if you use chisels from the _carver-cutter_. The chisel also functions as a [main-gauche](/Weapons.aspx?ID=32). All runes on the axe are replicated on the chisel, but only while both items are on the same person. You can Interact to reinsert the chisel.

**Activate—Chop Down** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ;  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** Make a Strike with the axe against a [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125) creature or a creature made primarily of wood. This Strike deals an additional 2d6 precision damage, and on a hit, the creature is [clumsy 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3) for 1 minute.

**Price** 850 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Wooden Breastplate](/Armor.aspx?ID=36)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Dozens of pictorial stories—told in wood carvings, painting, or pyrography—adorn every outer surface of this _+1 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [wooden breastplate](/Armor.aspx?ID=36)_. All are old, and many truly ancient, depicting tales set eons ago on the [Plane of Wood](/Planes.aspx?ID=25). You gain a +2 item bonus to [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) checks to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26). If you know the [_collective memories_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=15) ritual, you can use Nature instead of [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) if you're the primary caster.

**Activate—Statue Disguise** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The armor makes you look like a wooden statue version of one of the creatures depicted on the armor for 1 hour. This is a 3rd-rank [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=159), but it can make you look like any creature depicted on the armor. This doesn't change your size or the capabilities of your body, and it scales the appearance of the creature to match yours. You can Dismiss the activation. This disguise is just real enough to make you somewhat closer to a creature of wood. You're affected by two spells while it lasts: [_oaken resilience_](/Spells.aspx?ID=20) and [_speak with plants_](/Spells.aspx?ID=294). If you stand still, you gain a +2 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks and DCs to appear as an inanimate wooden statue, in addition to the status bonus to Deception from _illusory disguise_.

</row>

<row gap="medium">
