A patchwork of humanoid flesh makes up a _skinsaw mask_, which is stitched together with black silk or wire. It is distinctive for its bulbous orange eye—crafted from a magical glass bauble—and wide row of teeth. When worn, the mask amplifies your ability to sense fear in other creatures. You know the value of the [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) condition of any observed creature, and you gain a +1 item bonus to [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2040) checks to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) frightened creatures. Whenever you deal precision damage to a frightened creature, you deal 1 additional precision damage. If you aren’t [evil](/Traits.aspx?ID=64), you are [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) 2 while wearing a _skinsaw mask_.

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 180 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L --- Carved from a scale of the kaiju Igroon, this jagged shield refracts light around it in a shimmering haze. _A scale of Igroon_ ([Hardness](/Rules.aspx?ID=2183) 20, HP 160, BT 80) recovers 4 Hit Points at the start of its wielder’s turn. When you [Raise a Shield](/Actions.aspx?ID=2316), you can use the [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212) reaction with the scale of Igroon to block an attack or effect that deals [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=610), or [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) damage as well as physical damage. **Activate** Interact; **Requirements** You’re in an area of [bright](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402) or [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403); **Effect** You angle the shield to refract light. Until the start of your next turn, you gain a +4 item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) checks to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) and [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=2405) and can do so while observed. This bonus ends if you Activate another ability or use the [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212) reaction. **Activate** Interact; **Requirements** You’re in an area of bright light; **Effect** You angle the shield at a target within 60 feet, reflecting light into its eyes. It must attempt a DC 42 Fortitude save. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The target is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) until its next turn begins.
**Failure** The target is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 minute.
**Critical Failure** The target is blinded for 2d4 hours. **Activate** Interact; **Trigger** You use [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212) and prevent yourself from taking energy damage from a [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388), ray, or a direct attack, including a [_magic missile_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1536) spell; **Effect** You reflect the energy along a trajectory you choose. The effect travels only up to its remaining range, using its original parameters if it strikes other targets. **Destruction** If a deity, kaiju, spawn of a deity, titan, or being of similar power stomps on a _scale of Igroon_ while in absolute darkness, the shield is destroyed permanently.

markdown:
**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 180 **Usage** held in 2 hands **Bulk** 2 --- This _[+4 major striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [greater brilliant ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2833) [keen ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2843) [glaive](/Weapons.aspx?ID=375)_ binds the souls of powerful creatures it slays. The soul can’t be returned to life by any means while imprisoned within the glaive and can be freed only by a deed of great benevolence or selflessness. While using the glaive as a weapon, whenever you reduce a sapient creature of 18th level or higher to 0 Hit Points or roll a critical success with a Strike against such a target, the creature must attempt a DC 50 Fortitude save.**Critical Success** No additional effect.
**Success** The glaive siphons the creature’s essence, rendering it [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) 1. If the creature dies from the Strike or while drained in this way, the creature’s soul is bound in the glaive.
**Failure** As success, but the creature is drained 2.
**Critical Failure** As success, but the creature is drained 4. The glaive also has the following activations. **Activate** envision; **Trigger** You [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with the _Whisperer of Souls_; **Effect** You choose whether the Strike deals lethal or nonlethal damage. If the glaive has a reason for doing so, such as slaying a creature whose soul the glaive can absorb, it can defy your choice if you fail a DC 50 Will save. **Activate** envision; **Trigger** You attempt an [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) check to [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2363), [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=2365), [Learn a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2366), or [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367); **Effect** You listen to eldritch secrets the weapon whispers, gaining a +4 item bonus to the triggering check. **Activate** command, envision, Interact; **Frequency** once per week; **Effect** Attempt an [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) check as if you cast the [_legend lore_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=15) ritual about a subject. If you roll a success or critical success, you can repeat what the _Whisperer of Souls_ relates to you about the subject. On a critical failure, you and the glaive are drawn into a murmuring void of cold, where your mind is assaulted by strange visions for an entire week. At the end of this time, you reappear and must attempt a DC 50 Will save. **Success** When you return, you can retrain one of your skills into a [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) skill about evil creatures or places, as if you had spent 1 week retraining.
**Failure** As success, but you are [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 2 for 1 week.
**Critical Failure** As success, but your alignment moves one step toward evil and you must retrain one of your skills into a Lore about evil creatures or places. You become obsessed with increasing your forbidden knowledge, turning to wicked forces that offer such secrets and compromising your morals further if you must. **Destruction** If the _Whisperer of Souls_ is used to slay [Shelyn’s](/Deities.aspx?ID=293) herald, it disintegrates, bringing about great evil in its wake.

_Note from Nethys: This item is a constituent part of the [Ursine Avenger Hood](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=200) archetype using the [archetype artifact](/Rules.aspx?ID=1961) rules._

A gift passed from warrior to warrior, this cowl is made from a cave bear’s skull and fur. Once invested, the wearer gains a +1 item bonus to [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) checks to [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=2400), which increases to +2 if the animal is a [bear](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=370). The wearer of the hood feels a constant longing for the wilderness and wild places and takes a –1 item penalty to all [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=2391) or [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) if they go more than 5 days inside a large town or city without spending at least 4 hours in the wilderness.

**Destruction** Soak the _Ursine Avenger Hood_ in the blood of a [linnorm](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=439) that is at least 16th level and then burn it in a fire that uses only oak and chrysanthemum as fuel.

Forged in platinum, a _majordomo torc_ is engraved with heraldic insignias along with one language’s alphabet, much like a choker of elocution. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) checks and the ability to understand, speak, and write the torc’s language. Your excellent elocution reduces the DC of the [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333) to perform an auditory action while [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66) from 5 to 3. 

Upon being invested, the torc appoints itself your majordomo and, given the chance, takes over coordinating your social calendar, engagements, and wardrobe. A _majordomo torc_ has a prim, fussy disposition, and although it defers to you, it can grow sardonic if you frequently ignore its advice. The torc has the following activation.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The _majordomo torc_ casts [_befitting attire_](/Spells.aspx?ID=867) on you, usually to your specifications. However the torc can also choose the appearance of the [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629) for you.

item_bonus_note: Item bonus to Performance checks using the Piano
markdown:
**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 196 **Hands** 2 **Bulk** 16 --- **Perception** +22; precise vision 30 feet, [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=2407) hearing 30 feet **Communication** [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) (any languages the possessing spirit knew in life) **Skills** [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +23, [Music Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +23, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) +25, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +21 **Int** +3, **Wis** +4, **Cha** +5 **Will** +22 --- When a skilled musician dies before reaching their full potential or accomplishing an important goal, their soul might refuse to move on to the [Boneyard](/Planes.aspx?ID=39). Rather than becoming [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722), the spirit possesses an instrument they played in life, turning it into an intelligent item and a [virtuoso instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2737). (Other phantom instruments exist, but most are heavy.) A _phantom piano_ offers a bargain to any [bard](/Classes.aspx?ID=32) or other skilled musician who finds it: receive musical aid as you dedicate yourself to reaching the success the spirit felt they were denied in life. The piano refuses to play for those who reject this deal. If you accept, the piano asks only that you practice with it and perform for increasingly refined and august audiences, requiring a successful [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) check appropriate to your proficiency level. The piano sets no strict timeline, but at the GM’s discretion, if you go too long without making progress, the piano can cease cooperating with you until it’s satisfied with your dedication once again. While you keep up your end of the bargain, the piano grants you a +2 item bonus to Performance checks made with it. The piano also provides access to composition spells based on your Performance proficiency rank, as if you had the corresponding feat. The spells you can use comprise a cumulative list, but you can cast them only when using the piano. You must spend the actions and Focus Points required to cast these spells. **Trained:** [_inspire competence_](/Spells.aspx?ID=385), [_inspire courage_](/Spells.aspx?ID=386)
**Expert:** [_hymn of healing_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1768), [_inspire defense_](/Spells.aspx?ID=387)
**Master:** [_symphony of the unfettered heart_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1777)
**Legendary:** [_soothing ballad_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1776) A _phantom piano_ has the following activations. **Activate** command; **Effect** The piano shrinks down to a figurine of light Bulk compact enough to store in a pouch, or from figurine form back to instrument form. In figurine form, the piano doesn’t function as an instrument or provide magic other than this activation. **Activate** command; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can spend only to [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) the piano provides you.

item_bonus_note: Item bonus to Feint
markdown:
**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 204 **Usage** worn --- Blessed by [Nivi Rhombodazzle](/Deities.aspx?ID=354), this striking silver necklace is adorned with sparkling sapphires that draw the eye of any who see it. Over the years, this necklace has appeared in many paintings and illustrations, usually around the neck of a carefree and daring adventurer or a stylish rake gambling vast sums of coin. Finding this relic is always seen as a sign of great fortune to come, but when that luck runs out, the necklace is lost just as quickly. Wearing the relic, you quickly realize how distracting it can be, granting you a +1 item bonus on [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks made to [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=1434) and on [Games Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) checks made to gamble or determine the outcome of a game of chance. --- **Minor Gifts**: [beginner's luck](/Relics.aspx?ID=97), [whammy](/Relics.aspx?ID=99)
**Major Gifts**: [clean luck](/Relics.aspx?ID=100), [perception filter](/Relics.aspx?ID=52)
**Grand Gift**: [against all odds](/Relics.aspx?ID=102)
name: Fortune's Favor

item_bonus_note: Item bonus to Sense Motive
markdown:
**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 205 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L --- A famed detective once owned the long, curved _sleuth’s pipe_, taking it with them on investigations, keeping it in hand or mouth while cogitating. The pipe might have passed down through generations. Or, when an owner dies without heirs, it could go up for auction, be given to family friends, or remain at the scene of a crime to be found later. The _sleuth’s pipe_ has sapience that eventually awakens, allowing the relic to act as a helpful assistant in investigations. Even while this sapience sleeps within the pipe, it grants you a +1 item bonus to [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2040) checks to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302), and if you’re an [investigator](/Classes.aspx?ID=59), any checks you make to [Pursue a Lead](/Actions.aspx?ID=2811). --- **Minor Gifts**: [beginner's luck](/Relics.aspx?ID=97), [repository of knowledge](/Relics.aspx?ID=51)
**Major Gifts**: [intelligent relic](/Relics.aspx?ID=109), [steal luck](/Relics.aspx?ID=101)
**Grand Gift**: [mental bastion](/Relics.aspx?ID=54)

item_bonus_note: Item bonus to Recall Knowledge about historical events
markdown:
**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 205 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L --- The origins of the _watch of lost ages_, a silver pocket watch, are enigmatic. Its construction matches no known culture, and its appearance shifts back and forth from battered and tarnished to shiny and new without cause or apparent reason. The watch exudes a sense of melancholy and loss, and anyone holding it is acutely aware of the impermanence of all things and the march of time, moving ever forward. This relic might show up in a mysterious ruin or spontaneously appear in a spellcaster’s hand after they cast a [time](/Traits.aspx?ID=712) spell. The relic grants you a +1 item bonus to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about historical subjects. --- **Minor Gifts**: [fervor](/Relics.aspx?ID=93), [sands of the hourglass](/Relics.aspx?ID=104)
**Major Gifts**: [fervent spell](/Relics.aspx?ID=95), [temporal pulse](/Relics.aspx?ID=106)
**Grand Gift**: [time reversal](/Relics.aspx?ID=108)

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

---

These glasses have faceted red lenses like those of a mantis and are popular as a less ostentatious alternative to a full mask. While wearing the _gaze of the mantis_, your field of view increases to give you better awareness of your surroundings. You gain a +2 item bonus to visual Perception checks and cannot be [flanked](/Rules.aspx?ID=2375). 

**Activate—Target Sense** <actions string="Single Action" /> ;  **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You’re a Red Mantis assassin; **Effect** You learn the distance to and direction of all creatures that have a Red Mantis contract on them within 10 miles. If one of these creatures is within 100 feet, you also know any afflictions, conditions, and spells affecting them. This awareness lasts for 1 hour.

**Bulk** L

**Access** You're from the Mordant Spire

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

Made of petrified wood, this mask evokes the form of a coral reef. When you wear it, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks to [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381), and any armor you’re wearing gains the [aquadynamic](/Traits.aspx?ID=792) trait. 

**Activate—Cohabitate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** For 1 minute, your body becomes a mobile coral reef, letting much smaller creatures pass through or shelter in it. Creatures at least one size category smaller than you can share your space. Allies that share your space gain a +2 circumstance bonus to their AC, and you gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) 5 to any damage caused by a creature sharing the same space as you.

</column>

The swirls on this wooden mask—often worn by Mordant Censors—move and shift, reflecting the shape of the nearest currents. Wearing the mask grants you a +1 item bonus to [Sailing Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) and [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) checks. In addition, it allows you to pilot a boat with simply a thought. When you pilot a vehicle, you can keep both hands free and [Drive](/Actions.aspx?ID=3517) from any location on the vehicle. 

**Activate—Set the Course** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You are aboard a vehicle; **Effect** You become [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) for 1 minute or until you leave the vehicle, whichever comes first, and can use the extra action to [Take Control](/Actions.aspx?ID=3520) of the vehicle or, if you’re already piloting it, Drive or [Stop](/Actions.aspx?ID=3519) the vehicle.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 78

**Price** 2,600 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn mask

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access** You're from the Mordant Spire

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Carved concentric circles surround the eye and ear holes on this dark wooden mask, which lets you hear the whispers that fill the Mordant Spire. The barely audible susurrus that fills your ears advises you of peril, granting you a +1 item bonus to Perception checks for initiative and to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301), [Search](/Actions.aspx?ID=2630), or [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302) against things that intend harm to you, at the GM’s discretion, such as hostile creatures and haunts. If you tie a foe’s initiative roll, you go first. 

**Activate—Spire Power** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You are about to attempt a check that your mythic calling would allow you to spend a Mythic Point on;  **Effect** You draw on the power of the Mordant Spire. You gain 1 Mythic Point, which you can spend to attempt the check. If you don’t spend this point by the end of this turn, it is lost. You do not regain a Mythic Point if you critically succeed on the check, even if it’s the first time you did so that day, but still do so on the subsequent critical success, as usual. 

**Activate—Unforeseen Alert** <actions string="Free Action" /> ;    **Requirements** A creature or hazard you aren’t aware of targets you or includes you in an area effect, and you aren’t [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66); **Effect** The whispers warn you of the impending danger. You immediately gain a reaction that you can use only to respond to the triggering action or effect.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

This _[+1 ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2785) [explorer’s clothing](/Armor.aspx?ID=39)_ is a simple, practical, and unassuming two-piece outfit. The comfortable fabric is enchanted with illusory magic to make it look as if the wearer is wearing heavy armor (as _[_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1568)_). While wearing the suit, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388) someone who would normally wear heavy armor.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Age of Ashes</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />

<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />

**Source** [Pathfinder #147: Tomorrow Must Burn](/Sources.aspx?ID=8) pg. 71

**Price** 680 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 2

</row>

</column>

---

This mid-sized, silver cauldron is a boon within areas where access to fresh food is limited, for it can be commanded to fill itself with hearty (and delicious) vegetable stew. It can also be put to a much greater use in the pursuit of crafting certain items. When used to Craft alchemical items, potions, or oils, a bountiful cauldron grants a +2 item bonus to the Crafting check.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> command, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You stir the cauldron, and it casts a 4th-level [_create food_](/Spells.aspx?ID=52) spell, filling itself with enough delicious vegetable stew to feed 12 Medium creatures.

---

This pamphlet-sized book records the various symbols seen on fulus and also contains some ready-made magic on a special page that restores itself every day at sunrise. Using the compendium as a reference grants a +2 item bonus to any skill checks to determine a fulu’s function or authenticity. 

**Activate—Paralyzing Page** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You rip a page from the fulu compendium and cast it in a wide arc; as it flies in that arc, it multiplies into a storm of fulus. All [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) creatures in a 30-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) are affected by a _spirit-sealing fulu_ with a save DC of 25.

<title

    right="Item 6+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Insistent Door Knocker](/Equipment.aspx?ID=511)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 72

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This dark iron door knocker comes in a variety of shapes, such as a bird clutching a ring in its talons or a gargoyle holding a ring in its mouth. Placing the door knocker on the surface of a door (an Interact action) causes it to attach and remain in place. While in place, the door knocker whispers hints to you while you attempt to unlock the door, granting a +1 item bonus to [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) checks to Pick a Lock. Removing the door knocker from a surface requires you to use an Interact action.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You place the door knocker against a wall, floor, or ceiling. The door knocker fuses in place and creates a usable door within the surface. Any creature can move through the door normally, as if the door had always been there. The door can penetrate up to 1 foot of material, so thick material, such as heavy stone walls, can cause this effect to fail, expending its use for the day. A thin layer of metal in a wall, floor, or ceiling also causes the effect to fail. You can use an Interact action to release the door knocker from the surface and return the surface to its previous shape.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 18"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Archivist's Gaze](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5113)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Apex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=10" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 226

**Price** 24,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn eyepiece

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This strange contraption slides over your eyes, supernaturally sharpening your mind. While peering through it, you can feel some entity whispering to you, telling all sorts of things about the subject of your gaze. You gain a +3 item bonus to [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) (though some entities might grant a bonus to a different skill, as determined by your GM). In addition, when you employ an exploration tactic other than [Investigating](/Actions.aspx?ID=2627), you also gain the benefits of Investigating unless you choose not to. When you invest the spectacles, you either increase your Intelligence modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you the higher value. This gives you additional trained skills and languages, as normal for increasing your Intelligence modifier. You must select skills and languages the first time you invest the item, and whenever you invest the same _archivist’s gaze_, you get the same skills and languages you picked the first time. 

**Activate—Aid from Beyond** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** Adjusting the eyepiece’s focus and asking the entity for help, you cause the spectacles to cast either [_see the unseen_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663) or a 3rd-rank [_translate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1723) on you. Because the entity tied to the spectacles chooses which one, the GM picks whichever spell is most immediately useful in your current situation (and chooses the most useful language each time the item casts _translate_). The spell lasts for 1 minute.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>
name: Archivist's Gaze

markdown:
**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 226 **Price** 24,000 gp **Usage** worn mask **Bulk** L --- This mask appears to be a pool of mirrored, shifting silver adhered to a thin metal plate. When you place it against your face, it melds to the shape of your head. The material is breathable and light and doesn’t obscure vision. You gain a +2 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39), [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40), and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) checks while wearing the mask. When you [invest](/Rules.aspx?ID=3138) the mask, you either increase your Charisma modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value. **Activate—Shine of Silver** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You attempt a Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidation, or Performance check; **Effect** You gain a +4 status bonus to the triggering check. This ability has no effect if you’re under the effects of a disguise that hides the _mask of allure_. Depending on the skill used, the mirrored silver transforms into one of the following appearances.
**• [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38)** A swirl of silver, which entirely obscures and conceals your normal features.
**• [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39)** A kind, gentle, and inviting expression.
**• [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40)** An exaggerated visage of horror that shocks viewers into paying attention.
**• [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45)** A humanoid face, the mouth cracked wide with a comedic smile or a tragic frown, depending on the nature of the performance.
name: Mask of Allure

text: Item 18 Mask of Allure Apex Invested Magical Source Impossible Magic pg. 226 Price 24,000 gp Usage worn mask Bulk L This mask appears to be a pool of mirrored, shifting silver adhered to a thin metal plate. When you place it against your face, it melds to the shape of your head. The material is breathable and light and doesn’t obscure vision. You gain a +2 item bonus to Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidation, and Performance checks while wearing the mask. When you invest the mask, you either increase your Charisma modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value. Activate—Shine of Silver Free Action (concentrate, visual) Frequency once per day; Trigger You attempt a Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidation, or Performance check; Effect You gain a +4 status bonus to the triggering check. This ability has no effect if you’re under the effects of a disguise that hides the mask of allure . Depending on the skill used, the mirrored silver transforms into one of the following appearances. • Deception A swirl of silver, which entirely obscures and conceals your normal features. • Diplomacy A kind, gentle, and inviting expression. • Intimidation An exaggerated visage of horror that shocks viewers into paying attention. • Performance A humanoid face, the mouth cracked wide with a comedic smile or a tragic frown, depending on the nature of the performance.

The cloth feels smoother than silk, rippling and swaying like liquid when in motion. You feel a lively energy infusing your arms and legs. You gain a +3 item bonus to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) and [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) and a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against attacks from reactions triggered by your movement. When you [invest](/Rules.aspx?ID=3138) the cloak, you either increase your Dexterity modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value. **Activate—Cunning Dodge** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** An enemy misses you with a melee Strike; **Effect** You slip around the attacking creature with ease. You [Step](/Actions.aspx?ID=2304), without moving out of the triggering enemy’s reach, and then make a melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) against the triggering enemy if it’s within your reach. If you do make a Strike, the target attempts a DC 38 [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2040) check before you roll. **Failure** This creature is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) against the Strike.
**Critical Failure** This creature is off-guard against all your attacks until the end of its next turn. **Activate—Wandering Twirl** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), teleportation) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The cloak hums with power as your whirl it around yourself, disappearing amid a brief flash of light. Teleport up to double your [Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=1611) to a location you can see. At the end of the teleportation, you can make a melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) against a creature within reach, if there is one.

item_bonus_note: Item bonus while wearing the lash.
markdown:
**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 227 **Price** 24,000 gp **Usage** worn belt **Bulk** 1 --- The thin, glittering strands of rope that form this thick belt appear to be spun gold. Strung along the front of the belt are a collection of four multicolored, perfectly spherical beads: amethyst, jade, quartz, and turquoise. While wearing the lash, you gain a +3 item bonus to [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46). When you invest the belt, you either increase your Wisdom modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value. **Activate—Jewel of the Mind** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Effect** You touch one of the jewels affixed to the _sage’s lash_ and think the associated command word. Depending on the jewel, a different effect is produced that affects you and all living creatures in a 30-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387). After the effect occurs, all four jewels disappear from the lash, reappearing at the next dawn.
**• Amethyst** (light, revelation) Think “verity” to emit a magical trail of light from the lash that reveals the location of each creature in the emanation. For 1 round, if they would be [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83), they become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) instead, and if they would be [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96) or [unnoticed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=98) by a creature, they’re [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) instead. A creature can attempt a DC 43 [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) check to avoid the lash’s detection.
**• Jade** (healing) Think “purity” to produce a wave of green light that ends any [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) condition and any [persistent poison damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) affecting creatures in the emanation.
**• Quartz** (healing, vitality) Think “lenity” to have each creature regain 30 Hit Points.
**• Turquoise** Think “clarity” to grant all affected creatures a +2 status bonus to their next Will save for 1 minute.
name: Sage's Lash

markdown:
**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 227 **Price** 24,000 gp **Usage** worn gloves **Bulk** L --- These bronze gauntlets each have a small red gem embedded in the wrist. You gain a +3 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks and a +1 circumstance bonus to Athletics checks to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376). If you successfully Grapple an enemy that’s at least one size category larger than you, the gauntlets dig into it, dealing bludgeoning damage equal to your Strength modifier, plus an additional 2d6 on a critical success. When you invest the gloves, you either increase your Strength modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value. **Activate—Booming Clap** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697)) **Frequency** once per day; **Requirements** You have two hands free; **Effect** You clap the gauntlets together with a thunderous crack that deals 6d10 sonic damage in a 30-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387). Each creature in the area must attempt a DC 35 Fortitude save. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes half damage.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage and is [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66) for 1 round.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage, is deafened for 1 minute, and is [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) 1.

---

When opened, this grimoire has unlimited pages that, oddly, seem almost eager to transcribe spells. Unlike most grimoires, it has no limits to its number of spells. The grimoire’s eagerness to contain your spells grants you a +1 item bonus to checks to [Learn a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2366) if you do so by transcribing the spell into the grimoire. If you use the grimoire during your daily preparations and are capable of preparing spells of the appropriate rank, the grimoire’s nature leaks into your mind, allowing you to prepare an additional 1st-rank spell.

>
[Endless Grimoire](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5127)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Grimoire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=387" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 229

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When opened, this grimoire has unlimited pages that, oddly, seem almost eager to transcribe spells. Unlike most grimoires, it has no limits to its number of spells. The grimoire’s eagerness to contain your spells grants you a +1 item bonus to checks to [Learn a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2366) if you do so by transcribing the spell into the grimoire. If you use the grimoire during your daily preparations and are capable of preparing spells of the appropriate rank, the grimoire’s nature leaks into your mind, allowing you to prepare an additional 1st-rank spell.

markdown:
**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 73 **Usage** worn cloak **Bulk** 1 --- This long, shoddy cloak bears a hood and a simple brass clasp. While wearing the cloak, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to Impersonate an individual and to Lie while in character as that individual. **Activate** 1 minute (envision, Interact); **Frequency** once per day; **Requirements** You are Impersonating someone else; **Effect** While conversing or otherwise casually interacting with other creatures, you can adjust the mantle’s clasp to modify those creatures’ recollections of the last 5 minutes of their interaction with you. Each creature must attempt a DC 25 Will save. **Critical Success** The creature recalls the interaction clearly and realizes you were trying to alter their memory.
**Success** The creature recalls the interaction clearly.
**Failure** You decide whether or not the creature recalls the interaction. You can also alter minor details the creature recalls about the interaction, such as the time, place, and whether the interaction was favorable, as determined by the GM.
**Critical Failure** You decide whether or not the creature recalls the interaction. You can also alter major details the creature recalls about the interaction, such as believing you to be another individual or that the creature agreed to a favor, as determined by the GM. Unmemorable Mantle **Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 73 **Price** 300 gp **Bulk** 1 Unmemorable Mantle (Greater) **Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 73 **Price** 1,300 gp **Bulk** 1 --- The item bonus is +2, and the Will save DC is 28. Unmemorable Mantle (Major) **Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 73 **Price** 21,750 gp **Bulk** 1 --- The item bonus is +3, the Will save DC is 38, and you can activate the mantle once every 10 minutes.
name: Unmemorable Mantle

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 3"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Keymaking Tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5145)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 233

**Price** 55 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This [thieves’ toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2758) provides its owner the ability to have continued control over a lock while leaving it in place. It grants a +1 item bonus to [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) checks to [Pick a Lock](/Actions.aspx?ID=2412). Upon completely opening a lock by picking it with this toolkit, the toolkit produces a temporary copy of the key for the picked lock. This phantom key can lock or unlock the lock just like the original key. The key appears attached to the thieves’ toolkit by a fine silver chain and lasts for 12 hours before it fades into nothing. The _keymaking tools_ can only create and maintain one key at a time in this way; creating a new key replaces the previous one.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>
name: Keymaking Tools

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Thousand-Blade Thesis](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5146)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Extradimensional" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=67" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 233

**Price** 600 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This collection of lacquered rice paper scrolls mounted on flexible bamboo contains a wealth of calligraphic essays and paintings on the art of war, specifically focused on the use of various weapons in warfare and how to tactically deploy warriors using those weapons to the best possible advantage. Consulting the thesis grants a +2 item bonus to [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) checks to [Recall Knowledge](/Rules.aspx?ID=2638). Like most scholarly compendiums, this usage requires holding the thesis in one hand. The thesis also serves as an extradimensional armory for weapons and ammunition. The thesis has a capacity of 5 Bulk, and only weapons and ammunition can be stored within it. You and others can Interact with the thesis to store or retrieve a weapon or piece of ammunition in it, like a mundane container. 

**Activate—Instant Armory** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The _thousand-blade thesis_ dramatically unfurls, and the weapons contained within it spring forth and array themselves impressively in the air, floating within easy reach. For 1 minute, you can Interact as a free action to draw one of the floating weapons. Others can attempt to nab them out of the air, but to do so they must critically succeed at a [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=2383) check (DC 25). You can’t place weapons back into the thesis until the minute elapses.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>
name: Thousand-Blade Thesis

Activate—Instant Armory Single Action (manipulate) Frequency once per day; Effect The thousand-blade thesis dramatically unfurls, and the weapons contained within it spring forth and array themselves impressively in the air, floating within easy reach. For 1 minute, you can Interact as a free action to draw one of the floating weapons. Others can attempt to nab them out of the air, but to do so they must critically succeed at a Disarm check (DC 25). You can’t place weapons back into the thesis until the minute elapses.

>
[Sinister Knight](/Equipment.aspx?ID=518)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=92" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 92

**Price** 500 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto heavy armor

</row>

**Access** A character who is a member of the Knights of Lastwall has access to this option.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_Sinister knight_ armor shrouds the wearer’s identity in secrecy, allowing Crimson Reclaimers to pass among foes without being immediately unmasked. The wearer gains a +1 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;     **Effect** With a thought, the wearer activates a disguise. While the _sinister knight_ armor’s disguise is active, any identifying insignia or aesthetic of the armor is replaced by generic malevolent aesthetics such as spikes or demonic faces. While in the disguise, the wearer is always considered to be taking precautions against [lifesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=21), and even a creature that successfully notices the wearer with its lifesense mistakes the wearer for an undead unless it critically succeeds at its Perception check or the wearer critically fails a Deception or [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) check. Finally, while in the disguise, the rune attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=299) any effects that would reveal your alignment; on a successful counteract check, rather than negate the effect, the rune causes the effect to perceive your alignment as evil (maintaining any lawful or chaotic component of your alignment).

 The wearer can [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=74) the disguise, and if the wearer’s armor is removed, the disguise deactivates automatically.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<column gap="tiny">

**Bulk** L

---

These wire-rim glasses with large, circular lenses were invented for the sole purpose of avoiding awkward confrontations at social gatherings. They grant you a +1 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39). 

**Activate—Have We Met?** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** You stare at another creature and instantly remember their name if you've met and exchanged names. The glasses rely on your latent memories, so if the creature is disguising their identity, the glasses don't penetrate the disguise. For example, if a [divoynik](/Monsters.aspx?ID=4343) was disguised as an innkeeper you met, the glasses would give you the innkeeper's name, and if a noble you met before was in disguise as a masked vigilante, the glasses wouldn't reveal their true name.

>
[Hat of Many Minds](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5186)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 244

**Price** 1,800 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This pointy, brimmed hat is made up of a rainbow patchwork of various materials and seems to sit just a little lopsided on your head, no matter how you adjust it. You gain a +2 item bonus to checks to [Earn Income](/Actions.aspx?ID=2364) as the hat subtly helps with the tedious but important work that any given job might require. 

**Activate—Patchwork Double** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You tear off a patch of cloth to manifest it into a copy of yourself, dressed in your normal clothes, though they resemble the color and fabric of the patch. The copy follows your specific instructions and performs a single, straightforward task for up to 30 minutes. It takes the copy three times as long to complete the task as it would you, meaning it can perform a task that would take you a maximum of 10 minutes. It doesn’t react quickly enough to be of any use during an encounter, and it can’t use your spells or other special abilities—just basic actions and skill actions. The copy disappears and returns to the hat as a piece of cloth when the given task has been completed or when you [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) Patchwork Double.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 245

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When crafted, a _stampede medallion_ looks like nothing more than small silver disk, about the same size as a silver piece. When you invest this medallion for your eidolon, it changes shape to appear as a tiny, bejeweled facsimile of the eidolon, magically attached just over your eidolon’s heart. While your eidolon wears the medallion, they gain a +2 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=2382). 

**Activate—Impossible Tide** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Your eidolon momentarily manifests into a stampede of dozens of copies of themself. The stampede rampages out in every direction, swerving around your allies while trampling any foe on the ground in an [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) around your eidolon with a radius equal to your eidolon’s Speed. Each of these foes takes 8d6 bludgeoning damage, with a DC 29 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save. On a critical failure, the foe is also knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88). After dealing damage, the stampede of eidolons vanishes as quickly as it appeared.

May contain spoilers from Bastion of Blasphemies **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 239 **Price** 160 gp **Usage** worn belt --- This long, scarf-like garment appears to be made of living vines on which a dozen black roses bloom. While the vines appear to be thorny, they lack the capability to puncture or scratch, allowing the garland to be worn comfortably as a scarf or belt. The scent of the black roses evokes faint feelings of melancholy and nostalgia to the living, but undead find the odor to be unnerving and distracting. As long as you have a _graverose garland_ invested, it grants a +1 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) and [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks against undead. **Activate—To the Grave with You!** ([emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), manipulation, [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You lift some of the garland to your lips and blow, sending the scent of the black roses outward to target an undead creature you can see within 60 feet. The targeted undead becomes filled with the conviction that it belongs in its grave, and it must attempt a DC 19 Will save against the following effects. **Critical Success** The undead creature is unaffected.
**Success** The undead creature becomes [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the start of your next turn.
**Failure** The undead creature becomes [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 2 and is off-guard as long as it remains frightened.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but frightened 3, and the undead is also [fleeing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=74) as long as it remains frightened. If the undead knows of a nearby empty grave, it must flee toward that grave—if it enters the grave, it drops [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88) into the grave and remains prone until it is no longer frightened.
name: Graverose Garland

**Price** 500 gp

---

The _illusionist’s hat_ appears as a tall, black hat with a wide brim and a colorful band around its base. Although popularly associated with themes of magic, this hat is more the province of the entertainer or even the charlatan than of a proper arcanist, and many wizards scoff at those who openly wear such items. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks made to [Create a Diversion](/Actions.aspx?ID=2387) and to [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) checks made to [Palm an Object](/Actions.aspx?ID=2409). 

**Activate—What's In My Hat?** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** With a flourish, you remove your hat and sweep it before you. The _illusionist’s hat_ casts a 3rd-rank [_illusory creature_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1567) to your specifications, save that the creature created must be an animal. As long as you continue to hold your hat in one hand, you can Sustain this illusion as a free action. Unlike with most illusory creatures, you cannot use your actions to speak through the creature.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L  (when not activated)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

This miniature hunter’s lodge fits comfortably into the palm of one’s hand. 

**Activate—Expand Lodge** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You set the lodge on the ground, where it expands into a structure 40 feet long, 20 feet wide, and 20 feet high. The lodge is well-built, with a sturdy stone foundation, thick timber walls, and a peaked roof shingled with scraps of bark. The lodge’s ground floor contains a dining hall on one end and a sitting area with a hearth surrounded by comfortable chairs on the other. A staircase connects the hall to the lodge’s second floor, which consists of four simply furnished bedrooms. The lodge is decorated throughout with taxidermic beasts native to the Dimension of Dreams. If a creature inside the lodge spends 10 minutes studying these trophies, they gain a +3 item bonus to the next skill check they make in the next 24 hours to Recall Knowledge about any creature with the dream trait. Furnishings or decorations removed from the lodge disappear but return to their original locations inside the lodge with the next activation. You can [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) the dream hunter’s lodge to return it to its miniature form. 

**Activate—Oneiric Expedition** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** The _dream hunter’s lodge_ has been expanded and you are inside; **Effect** Spend 1 Mythic Point. You and all creatures inside the lodge fall into a magical slumber, and the lodge disappears from existence. After 8 hours, the lodge reappears in the Dimension of Dreams (or in the Universe, if the lodge was already in the Dimension of Dreams), as if transported there by an _interplanar teleport_ spell. Upon arrival, creatures inside the lodge awaken, fully rested (but this effect does not increase the number of times per day you can do your daily preparations).

_Deravon's helm_ is crafted with crown-like embellishments to give it an unmistakable air of authority. Crafted of gold with silver filigree incorporating images of swords, jewels, and most of all, the Eye of [Aroden](/Deities.aspx?ID=512) (from which the tines of the crown extend), _Deravon's helm_ is much lighter than would be expected. Downward swooping guards adorn the sides of the helm while leaving the face fully visible. It grants you a +1 item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks made to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395).

**Activate—Bow Before Aroden** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=642), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You issue a command to a humanoid within 30 feet to bow down before [Aroden's](/Deities.aspx?ID=512) glory. The targeted creature must make a DC 18 Will save to resist being compelled to drop [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88) as its first action on their next turn (on a critical failure, the target must spend all three actions on its next turn remaining prone). If the target is a [human](/Traits.aspx?ID=627), they take a –1 status penalty to the save.

The _mantle of far horizons_ helps to bring comfort and a sense of security while traveling, filling you with confidence and bolstering your energy during long journeys. In areas where you can see the horizon, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) checks made to [Sense Direction](/Actions.aspx?ID=2406).

**Activate—Gaze upon the Horizon** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You raise the mantle's hood to augment your ability to see over large distances or through adverse weather. For the next hour, or until you lower your hood (whichever comes first), you gain a +1 item bonus to Perception checks made to observe things more than 500 feet away, or while in [weather](/Traits.aspx?ID=464)-related conditions that penalize your Perception checks (such as [fog](/Rules.aspx?ID=815) or [precipitation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2816)).

**Activate—Listen to the World** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You lower the mantle's hood to focus on the world's natural sounds rather than other distractions. For the next minute, or until you raise the mantle's hood (whichever comes first), you gain a +1 item bonus to saving throws against [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) effects.

---

**_Nethys Note: This entry contains spoilers for The Dead God's Hand. Read at your own risk._**

The _Azlanti Diamond_ is among the most famous creations of the swordsmith (and eventual living god) [Aroden](/Deities.aspx?ID=512). Initially forged to serve as a badge of office for the next emperor of Azlant, this plan fell apart when King Xeros failed to choose his successor from a field of fools and criminals. When he asked Aroden for aid in choosing, the Last Azlanti chose to keep the _Azlanti Diamond_ for himself. Whether not this choice provoked the veiled masters into destroying Azlant with Earthfall or was the result of that doom forcing Aroden's hand has been lost to time—but PCs who take the Test of Aroden in this adventure have a good indication that it was a little bit of both! Following Earthfall, the Azlanti Diamond served Aroden for centuries. Now and then, he loaned the sword out to those he deemed worthy. Each time, the sword's power reset and then grew alongside its new carrier, eventually returning to Aroden's hand to begin the cycle anew. Some time after Aroden became a god and founded the city of Absalom, he bequeathed the sword to the caretakers of the Sanctum of Aroden, and for the past several thousand years it has remained therein.

The _Azlanti Diamond_ is a _[+1 striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=386)_. Its clear crystal blade is made of diamond, hardened to a strength equal to [highgrade throneglass](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5212) (although without the other qualities of high-grade throneglass). When first claimed by a character, it bonds with that character's soul, and as time passes the weapon's fundamental runes automatically grow in power, becoming a _+2 greater striking longsword_ after 1 year and finally a _+3 major striking longsword_ after it has been carried and wielded by the same person for 2 years. If the sword falls out of that character's possession it stops increasing in power until it is reclaimed, at which point the count begins where it left off. At your discretion, a PC can upgrade the weapon's fundamental runes normally, or they could even automatically progress not as time passes but as its wielder's level rises to match the corresponding fundamental runes.

As long as the _Azlanti Diamond_ is carried, its wielder can speak and understand ancient [Azlanti](/Languages.aspx?ID=49), and they gain a +1 item bonus to [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37), and [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks. These item bonuses increase to +2 once the wielder is 9th level, then increase again to +3 once the wielder is 17th level.

Unlike the standard rules for a [specific weapon](/Rules.aspx?ID=3179), the _Azlanti Diamond_ can be etched with weapon property runes. Etching a weapon property rune onto the _Azlanti Diamond_ is free—it never costs money to etch a rune onto this artifact.

---

**Minor Gifts:** [divine retribution](/Relics.aspx?ID=136), [recalculate](/Relics.aspx?ID=173) 

**Major Gifts:** [psychic scream](/Relics.aspx?ID=176), [sacred glow](/Relics.aspx?ID=140) 

**Grand Gift:** [mental bastion](/Relics.aspx?ID=177) 

The _Azlanti Diamond_ is never less than an 8th-level item, and as its wielder gains levels, it gains levels to match—a wielder who is higher than 8th level causes the _Azlanti Diamond_ to automatically rise in level to match. This means it always has its two minor gifts active. It gains its first major gift at 9th level, and its second at 13th level, then gains its grand gift at 17th level. These gifts are gained automatically, without the need to achieve any additional requirement.

**Destruction** The _Azlanti Diamond_ is destroyed if it is used in an attempt to shatter the _Starstone_ by a [human](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=64) who wasn't born as a human and has never heard of Aroden.

Initially forged to serve as a badge of office for the next emperor of Azlant, this plan fell apart when King Xeros failed to choose his successor from a field of fools and criminals. When he asked Aroden for aid in choosing, the Last Azlanti chose to keep the _Azlanti Diamond_ for himself. Following Earthfall, the Azlanti Diamond served Aroden for centuries. Now and then, he loaned the sword out to those he deemed worthy. Each time, the sword's power reset and then grew alongside its new carrier, eventually returning to Aroden's hand to begin the cycle anew. Some time after Aroden became a god and founded the city of Absalom, he bequeathed the sword to the caretakers of the Sanctum of Aroden, and for the past several thousand years it has remained therein.

The _Azlanti Diamond_ is a _[+1 striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=386)_. Its clear crystal blade is made of diamond, hardened to a strength equal to [highgrade throneglass](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5212) (although without the other qualities of high-grade throneglass). When first claimed by a character, it bonds with that character's soul, and as time passes the weapon's fundamental runes automatically grow in power, becoming a _+2 greater striking longsword_ after 1 year and finally a _+3 major striking longsword_ after it has been carried and wielded by the same person for 2 years. If the sword falls out of that character's possession it stops increasing in power until it is reclaimed, at which point the count begins where it left off. At your discretion, a PC can upgrade the weapon's fundamental runes normally, or they could even automatically progress not as time passes but as its wielder's level rises to match the corresponding fundamental runes.

As long as the _Azlanti Diamond_ is carried, its wielder can speak and understand ancient [Azlanti](/Languages.aspx?ID=49), and they gain a +1 item bonus to [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37), and [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks. **_Nethys Note: This entry contains spoilers for The Dead God's Hand. Read at your own risk._**

The _Azlanti Diamond_ is among the most famous creations of the swordsmith (and eventual living god) [Aroden](/Deities.aspx?ID=512). Initially forged to serve as a badge of office for the next emperor of Azlant, this plan fell apart when King Xeros failed to choose his successor from a field of fools and criminals. When he asked Aroden for aid in choosing, the Last Azlanti chose to keep the _Azlanti Diamond_ for himself. Whether not this choice provoked the veiled masters into destroying Azlant with Earthfall or was the result of that doom forcing Aroden's hand has been lost to time—but PCs who take the Test of Aroden in this adventure have a good indication that it was a little bit of both! Following Earthfall, the Azlanti Diamond served Aroden for centuries. Now and then, he loaned the sword out to those he deemed worthy. Each time, the sword's power reset and then grew alongside its new carrier, eventually returning to Aroden's hand to begin the cycle anew. Some time after Aroden became a god and founded the city of Absalom, he bequeathed the sword to the caretakers of the Sanctum of Aroden, and for the past several thousand years it has remained therein.

The _Azlanti Diamond_ is a _[+1 striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=386)_. Its clear crystal blade is made of diamond, hardened to a strength equal to [highgrade throneglass](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5212) (although without the other qualities of high-grade throneglass). When first claimed by a character, it bonds with that character's soul, and as time passes the weapon's fundamental runes automatically grow in power, becoming a _+2 greater striking longsword_ after 1 year and finally a _+3 major striking longsword_ after it has been carried and wielded by the same person for 2 years. If the sword falls out of that character's possession it stops increasing in power until it is reclaimed, at which point the count begins where it left off. At your discretion, a PC can upgrade the weapon's fundamental runes normally, or they could even automatically progress not as time passes but as its wielder's level rises to match the corresponding fundamental runes.

As long as the _Azlanti Diamond_ is carried, its wielder can speak and understand ancient [Azlanti](/Languages.aspx?ID=49), and they gain a +1 item bonus to [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37), and [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks. These item bonuses increase to +2 once the wielder is 9th level, then increase again to +3 once the wielder is 17th level.

Unlike the standard rules for a [specific weapon](/Rules.aspx?ID=3179), the _Azlanti Diamond_ can be etched with weapon property runes. Etching a weapon property rune onto the _Azlanti Diamond_ is free—it never costs money to etch a rune onto this artifact.

---

**Minor Gifts:** [divine retribution](/Relics.aspx?ID=136), [recalculate](/Relics.aspx?ID=173) 

**Major Gifts:** [psychic scream](/Relics.aspx?ID=176), [sacred glow](/Relics.aspx?ID=140) 

**Grand Gift:** [mental bastion](/Relics.aspx?ID=177) 

The _Azlanti Diamond_ is never less than an 8th-level item, and as its wielder gains levels, it gains levels to match—a wielder who is higher than 8th level causes the _Azlanti Diamond_ to automatically rise in level to match. This means it always has its two minor gifts active. It gains its first major gift at 9th level, and its second at 13th level, then gains its grand gift at 17th level. These gifts are gained automatically, without the need to achieve any additional requirement.

**Destruction** The _Azlanti Diamond_ is destroyed if it is used in an attempt to shatter the _Starstone_ by a [human](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=64) who wasn't born as a human and has never heard of Aroden.

This bracelet resembles a string of pearls filled with swirling air, making you more buoyant. While wearing the bracelet, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks to Swim. 

**Activate—Float** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You’re submerged in water or another liquid; **Effect** You rapidly surface, rising 60 feet at the end of each of your turns. Once you reach the liquid’s surface, you can’t dive or sink for the next 10 minutes, and a creature that attempts to pull you beneath the surface must first succeed at a DC 17 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check.

**Access** You’re a member of the Order of the Torrent.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The Order of the Torrent works to rescue kidnapped people, and their cobalt blue badge can often open doors that would otherwise be closed. When wearing this badge, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) and [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks to [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=2408) or Gather Information about a missing person. 

**Activate—Modus Operandi** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** A kidnapping occurred within 15 feet of your location, or you have some information about the target or perpetrators of a kidnapping; **Effect** You attempt to Recall Knowledge about those who perpetrated the kidnapping, the information supernaturally surfacing in your mind. The GM determines what skill and DC to use for this check based on the level and nature of the perpetrators (usually a [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) check at a standard DC for the perpetrator’s level). In addition, if you fail to Recall Knowledge about the kidnapper (but don’t critically fail), you eliminate one false lead about the kidnapper or how they abducted the target. For instance, you might determine that an incorporeal undead wasn’t involved, though you gain no other information about what happened. The mark can’t provide specific identifying information about the perpetrators, like their name or location.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

Activate—Modus Operandi Single Action (concentrate) Frequency once per day; Requirements A kidnapping occurred within 15 feet of your location, or you have some information about the target or perpetrators of a kidnapping; Effect You attempt to Recall Knowledge about those who perpetrated the kidnapping, the information supernaturally surfacing in your mind. The GM determines what skill and DC to use for this check based on the level and nature of the perpetrators (usually a Society check at a standard DC for the perpetrator’s level). In addition, if you fail to Recall Knowledge about the kidnapper (but don’t critically fail), you eliminate one false lead about the kidnapper or how they abducted the target. For instance, you might determine that an incorporeal undead wasn’t involved, though you gain no other information about what happened. The mark can’t provide specific identifying information about the perpetrators, like their name or location.

This dark, withered wood armor is crafted from the tree left behind when a dryad dies. Every step in crafting is a race to seal the magic inside before the wood rots away. The result is a _[+1](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2804) [wooden breastplate](/Armor.aspx?ID=36)_ that looks to be made of eternally decaying wood. The twisted nature of your armor allows you to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) animals and plants without taking a penalty if the creature doesn't understand your language. 

**Activate—Peel Bark** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You peel away a layer of dead wood. Attempt a flat check to end any [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) affecting your exterior (such as being on fire) as though you had an assisted recovery.

**Bulk** 4
</row>

<row gap="medium">

---

Usually made of hardwood such as oak or ash, a _weaver’s wheel_ is a finely crafted spinning wheel. This device spins thread until its supply runs out. Should the bobbin of the spinning wheel fill, however, the wheel will cease to function until the bobbin is replaced. In addition to mundane thread, more mystical materials can be spun as well. The wheel has 20 Hit Points (BT 10) and a Hardness of 5. Particularly harsh materials, such as basilisk sinew or copper, can swiftly wear the wheel down, causing 1d6 bludgeoning damage (ignoring Hardness) to the wheel for every bobbin used. Using a _weaver’s wheel_ to assist with the Craft downtime activity grants a +1 item bonus to [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) checks associated with weaving and clothing fabrication.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Vaultlines</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=537" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #225: Vaultlines](/Sources.aspx?ID=381) pg. 221

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When imbibed, the herbal wine created by this enchanted, golden goblet aids in spells and rituals designed to transfer memories, though sometimes at a steep price. Any liquid created by the goblet evaporates if not consumed within 1 minute. 

**Activate—Awaken Ancestral Memory** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The goblet fills with a foul-tasting but potent herbal wine. When used as a part of the cost of the _[recall past life](/Rituals.aspx?ID=228)_ ritual, the wine grants a +3 item bonus to skill checks made to cast the ritual. After the ritual is complete, the next time each caster (but not the imbiber) falls asleep, they must attempt a DC 34 Will save against the effects of the _[nightmare](/Spells.aspx?ID=1615)_ spell, as [Yig](/Deities.aspx?ID=579) sends horrific visions of writhing serpents to disturb their slumber. A creature that fails the saving throw must repeat the save each night until they succeed. 

**Activate—Share Memory** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You think of a particular memory, which the goblet transforms into a _[potion of shared memories](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2952)._ A creature that drinks this potion gains a +1 item bonus to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) in a skill of your choice in which you're trained. If you're expert in the skill, the item bonus increases to +2. If you're master, the bonus increases to +3, and if you're legendary, the bonus increases to +4. This bonus lasts for 1 hour. 

**Activate—Drink and Hiss** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You drink from the goblet, imbuing your breath with Yig's omens, and then exhale. All creatures in a 15-foot emanation must make a DC 34 Fortitude save against the effects of _[mindfog mist](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3341)._ A creature that doesn't worship Yig takes 3d6 [persistent mental damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) for as long as they remain poisoned by this effect.

**Destruction** If a creature holding the _Venom of Memories_ is swallowed whole by Yig or one of his divine servants, the goblet melts and is destroyed.

</column>

text: Item 15 Venom Of Memories May contain spoilers from Vaultlines Unique Artifact Divine Source Pathfinder #225: Vaultlines pg. 221 Usage held in 1 hand When imbibed, the herbal wine created by this enchanted, golden goblet aids in spells and rituals designed to transfer memories, though sometimes at a steep price. Any liquid created by the goblet evaporates if not consumed within 1 minute. Activate—Awaken Ancestral Memory Two Actions (concentrate, manipulate) Frequency once per day; Effect The goblet fills with a foul-tasting but potent herbal wine. When used as a part of the cost of the recall past life ritual, the wine grants a +3 item bonus to skill checks made to cast the ritual. After the ritual is complete, the next time each caster (but not the imbiber) falls asleep, they must attempt a DC 34 Will save against the effects of the nightmare spell, as Yig sends horrific visions of writhing serpents to disturb their slumber. A creature that fails the saving throw must repeat the save each night until they succeed. Activate—Share Memory Two Actions (concentrate, manipulate) Frequency once per day; Effect You think of a particular memory, which the goblet transforms into a potion of shared memories. A creature that drinks this potion gains a +1 item bonus to Recall Knowledge in a skill of your choice in which you're trained. If you're expert in the skill, the item bonus increases to +2. If you're master, the bonus increases to +3, and if you're legendary, the bonus increases to +4. This bonus lasts for 1 hour. Activate—Drink and Hiss Two Actions (concentrate, manipulate) Frequency once per day; Effect You drink from the goblet, imbuing your breath with Yig's omens, and then exhale. All creatures in a 15-foot emanation must make a DC 34 Fortitude save against the effects of mindfog mist. A creature that doesn't worship Yig takes 3d6 persistent mental damage for as long as they remain poisoned by this effect. Destruction If a creature holding the Venom of Memories is swallowed whole by Yig or one of his divine servants, the goblet melts and is destroyed.

May contain spoilers from Vaultlines **Source** [Pathfinder #225: Vaultlines](/Sources.aspx?ID=381) pg. 222 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L --- Over the eons, master artisans have used imperfect copies of the _Artifex Telluria_ to craft all manner of earthen wonders. The true _Artifex Telluria_ is a legend even among xiomorns, a tool of peerless quality supposedly used by Sairazul herself to shape the first of her children from living rock. This storied artifact is believed to be one of the few implements capable of employing the equally legendary _Tectonic Forge_ to craft a vessel worthy of housing the spirit of a vault builder.

When the _artifex_ is used to create or repair constructs, structures, or other objects composed mostly or entirely of stone, crystal, or other earthen materials, it reduces overall crafting time by half and grants a +2 item bonus to [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) checks. **Activate—Earthwright** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Effect** Over the course of 1 minute, you sculpt up to a 10-foot cube of earth or stone into a new form, with the effects of _[shape stone](/Spells.aspx?ID=1667)_. Artifex Telluria (Minor) **Source** [Pathfinder #225: Vaultlines](/Sources.aspx?ID=381) pg. 222 **Price** 700 gp Artifex Telluria (Lesser) **Source** [Pathfinder #225: Vaultlines](/Sources.aspx?ID=381) pg. 222 **Price** 6,500 gp --- You can use your [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) or [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) skill in place of [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) when the _artifex_ is used to create or repair constructs, structures, or other objects composed mostly or entirely of stone, crystal, or other earthen materials. In addition, the _lesser artifex telluria_ has the Stonecalling activation. **Activate—Stonecalling** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You use the _artifex_ to channel the geomantic energies that course through the ground beneath your feet. You cast either a 7th-rank _[summon elemental](/Spells.aspx?ID=1698)_ ([earth elementals](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=409) only) or 7th-rank _[wall of stone](/Spells.aspx?ID=1751)_. Artifex Telluria May contain spoilers from Vaultlines **Source** [Pathfinder #225: Vaultlines](/Sources.aspx?ID=381) pg. 222 --- The [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) bonus increases to +3. In addition, the _Artifex Telluria_ has the Terrafusion activation. **Activate—Terrafusion** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Effect** You spend 12 hours and a quantity of rare materials to prepare a specially constructed stone or crystalline vessel and imbue it with unbound elemental essence, creating any elemental earth creature of your level or lower, with a maximum level of 17. If the elemental is at least 4 levels lower than you, you can make it a minion; otherwise, it’s friendly to you. Completing the vessel requires a successful DC 44 [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) check and raw materials worth 2,000 gp per level of the creature. On a critical success, you reduce the material requirements by half; on a failure or critical failure, you are unsuccessful and can’t try again for 1 day. Alternatively, you can attempt to imbue the vessel with the fading spirit of a willing elemental earth creature that has died within the past month. The Crafting DC and material costs remain the same, but the creature’s disposition toward you is not predetermined, and you can’t make it a minion unless it was already your minion at its time of death.
name: Artifex Telluria (Minor)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />

**Price** 10,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This magical chisel evokes the holy symbol of the elven goddess of art and architecture, Findeladlara. The _Guiding Chisel’s_ original function was as a portal key to Duskgate, but as Alseta’s Ring faded from the collective memories of the elves, the chisel became known and used exclusively for its other abilities. Eventually, elven emissaries gave it to the dwarves of Saggorak as a gesture of friendship.

 You gain a +3 item bonus to Crafting checks related to stonemasonry. In addition, it takes you only 1 day to Craft items using the _Guiding Chisel_ instead of 4 days, and you quadruple the discount you get for spending additional days Crafting items with the _Guiding Chisel_. If it’s unclear whether you could use the _Guiding Chisel_ to Craft an item, the GM decides.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (command, envision, Interact);  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You embed the _Guiding Chisel_ in the ground and imagine a building. After 10 minutes, you remove the chisel and the building appears. The building can take any shape you wish, filling up to ten contiguous 10-foot cubes within 1,000 feet of the chisel. The building lasts until you use the chisel to create another building. This building has the [structure](/Traits.aspx?ID=153) trait.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>
